sentences.zh: 完顏素蘭

translations.literal: Wanyan Sulan
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sulan

sentences.zh: 七月，車駕至汴，素蘭上書言事，略曰：「昔東海在位，信用讒諂，疏斥忠直，以致小人日進，君子日退，紀綱紊亂，法度益隳。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when the imperial procession arrived at Bian, Sulan submitted a memorial on affairs of state, in summary saying: "In the past when the Marquis of Donghai held the throne, he trusted slander and flattery, kept loyal and upright men at a distance, so that petty men advanced day by day while gentlemen retreated day by day, the institutional framework was in disorder, and laws and regulations were further destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, when the imperial procession reached Bian, Sulan submitted a memorial on state affairs, in summary saying: "When the Marquis of Donghai still held the throne, he trusted slanderers and flatterers and kept loyal, upright men at arm's length, so petty men advanced day by day while gentlemen fell back day by day, institutions fell into disorder, and the laws were further undone.

sentences.zh: 風折城門之關，火焚市里之舍，蓋上天垂象以儆懼之也。

translations.literal: The wind broke the gate-bars of the city walls, fire burned the houses in the market wards—surely Heaven was displaying omens to warn and alarm him.
translations.idiomatic: The wind snapped the city gate-bars, fire consumed houses in the market wards—surely Heaven was sending omens to warn and alarm him.

sentences.zh: 言者勸其親君子、遠小人、恐懼修省，以答天變，東海不從，遂至亡滅。

translations.literal: Advisers urged him to draw close to gentlemen and keep petty men at a distance, to fear and cultivate himself in reform so as to answer Heaven's changes, but the Marquis of Donghai did not follow this, and thus came to ruin and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged him to draw near to gentlemen, keep petty men at a distance, and reform himself in fear and vigilance to answer Heaven's warnings, but the Marquis of Donghai would not listen, and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫善救亂者必跡其亂之所由生，善革弊者必究其弊之所自起，誠能大明黜陟以革東海之政，則治安之效可指日而待也。

translations.literal: One who is good at rescuing disorder must trace where the disorder arose; one who is good at reforming abuses must thoroughly investigate whence the abuses themselves originated. If Your Majesty can with full clarity advance and dismiss officials to reform the government of the Marquis of Donghai's time, then the effect of peace and good order could be awaited within days.
translations.idiomatic: Those skilled at rescuing disorder must trace where disorder began; those skilled at reforming abuses must probe to their source. If Your Majesty can with full clarity promote and dismiss officials and reform the policies of the Marquis of Donghai's reign, the fruits of peace and order could be awaited within days.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，不思出此，輒議南遷，詔下之日，士民相率上章請留，啟行之日，風雨不時、橋樑數壞，人心天意亦可見矣。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty rose to the throne, instead of reflecting on this, you at once deliberated on moving south. On the day the edict was issued, scholars and commoners in succession submitted memorials asking you to stay; on the day the procession set out, wind and rain were untimely and bridges repeatedly broke—the mind of the people and the will of Heaven can also be seen thereby.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, instead of reflecting on this lesson you at once debated moving the capital south. On the day the edict was issued, scholars and commoners submitted memorial after memorial begging you to stay; on the day the procession set out, wind and rain came at the wrong season and bridges broke again and again—the hearts of the people and the will of Heaven were plain enough.

sentences.zh: 此事既往，豈容複追，但自今尤宜戒慎，覆車之轍不可引轅而複蹈也。」

translations.literal: This matter is already past—how could it be pursued again? But from now on all the more should one be cautious and warn oneself: the rut of an overturned cart cannot have its shafts dragged through it and be trodden again."
translations.idiomatic: That episode is past and cannot be undone, but from this day forward all the more must we be on guard: one cannot hitch the shafts to an overturned cart's rut and drive through it again."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「國家不可一日無兵，兵不可一日無食。

translations.literal: He also said: "The state cannot be without troops for a single day, nor can troops be without provisions for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "A state cannot go a single day without soldiers, nor can soldiers go a single day without food.

sentences.zh: 陛下為社稷之計，宮中用度皆從貶損，而有司複多置軍官，不恤妄費，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of soil and grain, has reduced all palace expenditures, yet the responsible offices have again appointed many additional military officers, heedless of reckless expenditure—this is very pointless.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, has cut palace expenditures to the bone, yet the responsible offices keep appointing more military officers and heed reckless spending—this is utterly pointless.

sentences.zh: 或謂軍官之眾所以張大威聲，臣竊以為不然。

translations.literal: Some say the multitude of military officers is meant to magnify prestige and authority; your subject ventures to think this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say a host of military officers is meant to magnify our prestige; your subject does not believe it.

sentences.zh: 不加精選而徒務其多，緩急臨敵其可用乎？

translations.literal: If you do not carefully select them but only pursue their numbers, when urgency comes and you face the enemy, can they be used?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not select them carefully but only chase numbers, when crisis comes and we face the enemy, will they be of any use?

sentences.zh: 且中都惟其糧乏，故使車駕至此。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the Central Capital grain alone was scarce, and therefore the imperial procession was sent here.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, grain alone was scarce at the Central Capital, which is why the imperial procession was sent here.

sentences.zh: 稍獲安地，遂忘其危而不之備，萬一再如前日，未知有司複請陛下何之也。」

translations.literal: Having slightly obtained a secure place, you then forgot the danger and did not prepare for it—if once again it should be as on the former day, it is not known what responsible offices would again request that Your Majesty go whither."
translations.idiomatic: Having gained a slightly safer place, you then forgot the danger and made no preparations—if once again things should be as on that former day, who knows whither the responsible offices would again ask Your Majesty to flee?"

sentences.zh: 三年正月，素蘭自中都計議軍事回，上書求見，乞屏左右。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Sulan returned from the Central Capital where he had been planning military affairs, submitted a memorial requesting audience, and begged to dismiss all attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Sulan returned from planning military affairs at the Central Capital, submitted a memorial requesting audience, and asked that all attendants be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上遣人諭之曰：「屏人奏事，朕固常爾。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to instruct him, saying: "Presenting memorials with attendants dismissed is something I customarily do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to instruct him: "Receiving memorials with attendants dismissed is something I do routinely.

sentences.zh: 近以遊茂因緣生疑間之語，故凡有所引見，必令一近臣立侍，汝有封章，亦無患不密也。

translations.literal: Recently, because You Mao gave rise to suspicious words through some opportune connection, whenever anyone is brought in for audience I must have one close attendant stand in attendance. If you have a sealed memorial, there is also no worry that it will not be kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because You Mao stirred up suspicious talk through some opportune connection, whenever anyone is brought in for audience I require one close attendant to stand by. If you have a sealed memorial, there is no fear it will not be kept secret.

sentences.zh: 」尋召至近侍局，給紙劄令書所欲言，書未及半，上出禦便殿見之，悉去左右，惟近侍局直長趙和和在焉。

translations.literal: " Soon after he was summoned to the Bureau of Palace Attendants, was given paper and told to write what he wished to say. Before half the writing was finished, the emperor came out to the Imperial Convenience Hall to see him, dismissed all attendants entirely, and only Zhao Hehe, direct supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, remained there.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after he was summoned to the Bureau of Palace Attendants and given paper to write what he wished to say. Before he had finished half the sheet, the emperor came out to the Imperial Convenience Hall to see him, dismissed every attendant, and only Zhao Hehe, direct supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, remained.

sentences.zh: 素蘭奏曰：「臣聞興衰治亂有國之常，在所用之人如何耳。

translations.literal: Sulan memorialized, saying: "Your subject has heard that rise and fall, order and disorder are constants of any state—they depend on the sort of men employed.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan memorialized: "Your subject has heard that rise and fall, order and disorder are constants of any state—it all depends on what sort of men are employed.

sentences.zh: 用得其人，雖衰亂尚可扶持，一或非才，則治安亦亂矣。

translations.literal: If the right men are employed, even in decline and disorder the state can still be sustained; if it happens that one is not talented, then even in peace and order there will still be disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Employ the right men and even decline and disorder can still be shored up; employ the wrong man and even peace and order will turn to chaos.

sentences.zh: 向者颭軍之變，中都帥府自足剿滅，朝廷乃令移剌刺塔不也等招誘之，使帥府不敢盡其力，既不能招，愈不可制矣。

translations.literal: Previously, at the mutiny of the Gust Troops, the Central Capital Military Command was itself sufficient to suppress and destroy them, yet the court ordered Yila Chitabuye and others to entice them to surrender, so that the military command dared not exert its full strength; when they could not be enticed, they became all the harder to control.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gust Troops mutinied, the Central Capital Military Command was itself sufficient to suppress them, yet the court ordered Yila Chitabuye and others to entice them to surrender, so the command dared not exert its full strength; when enticement failed, they became all the harder to control.

sentences.zh: 至於伯德文哥之叛，帥府方議削其權，而朝廷傳旨俾領義軍，文哥由是益肆，改除之令輒拒不受，不臣之狀亦顯矣。

translations.literal: As for Bo'de Wenge's rebellion: when the military command was just deliberating curtailing his authority, the court transmitted an edict ordering him to command the Loyalist Army, and Wenge thereby became all the more unrestrained—when transfer appointments were issued he bluntly refused to accept them, and his disposition as a non-subject also became obvious.
translations.idiomatic: As for Bo'de Wenge's rebellion: when the military command was deliberating curtailing his authority, the court transmitted an edict ordering him to command the Loyalist Army, and Wenge grew all the bolder—when transfer orders were issued he refused them outright, and his disloyalty was plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 帥府方且收捕，而朝廷複赦之，且不令隸帥府。

translations.literal: When the military command was about to arrest him, the court again pardoned him and moreover would not let him be subordinate to the military command.
translations.idiomatic: When the military command was about to arrest him, the court pardoned him again and would not even let him remain under the command's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 國家付方面於重臣，乃不信任，顧養叛賊之奸，不知誰為陛下畫此計者。

translations.literal: The state entrusts a frontier to a high minister yet does not trust him, but instead nurtures the treachery of rebels—who, I wonder, drew up this plan for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: The state entrusts a frontier to a great minister yet does not trust him, but instead nurtures the treachery of rebels—who, I wonder, devised this plan for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 臣自外風聞，皆平章高琪之意，惟陛下裁察。

translations.literal: Your subject from outside has heard by rumor that it was all the intention of Grand Councilor Gao Qi—may Your Majesty investigate and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard from outside that it was all the doing of Grand Councilor Gao Qi—may Your Majesty investigate and judge.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝言皆是。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What you say is all correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Everything you say is correct.

sentences.zh: 文哥之事，朕所未悉，誠如所言，朕肯赦之乎？

translations.literal: As for Wenge's affair, I was not yet fully informed; if it is truly as you say, would I consent to pardon him?
translations.idiomatic: As for Wenge's affair, I was not yet fully informed; if it is truly as you say, would I have pardoned him?

sentences.zh: 且汝何以知此事出於高琪？

translations.literal: Moreover, how do you know this affair came from Gao Qi?
translations.idiomatic: And how do you know this affair came from Gao Qi?

sentences.zh: 」素蘭曰：「臣見文哥牒永清副提控劉溫雲：'所差人張希韓至自南京，道副樞平章處分，已奏令文哥隸大名行省，勿複遵中都帥府約束'。

translations.literal: " Sulan said: "Your subject saw Wenge's dispatch to Yongqing deputy commander Liu Wenyun: 'The man Zhang Xihan whom you sent arrived from Nanjing and stated the disposition of the Deputy Commander of the Military Affairs Commission and Grand Councilor—already memorialized to order Wenge subordinate to the Daming Branch Secretariat, no longer to follow constraints of the Central Capital Military Command.'
translations.idiomatic: " Sulan said: "Your subject saw Wenge's dispatch to Yongqing deputy commander Liu Wenyun: 'The man Zhang Xihan whom you sent arrived from Nanjing and reported the disposition of the Deputy Commander of the Military Affairs Commission and Grand Councilor—already memorialized to place Wenge under the Daming Branch Secretariat and no longer subject to the Central Capital Military Command's constraints.'

sentences.zh: 溫即具言于帥府。

translations.literal: Wen immediately reported this in full to the military command.
translations.idiomatic: Wen immediately reported this in full to the military command.

sentences.zh: 然則，罪人與高琪計結明矣。

translations.literal: In that case, the criminal and Gao Qi's plotting are entirely clear.
translations.idiomatic: In that case, the criminal's collusion with Gao Qi is entirely clear.

sentences.zh: 」上頷之。

translations.literal: " The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 素蘭續奏曰：「高琪本無勳勞，亦無公望，向以畏死故擅誅胡沙虎，蓋出無聊耳。

translations.literal: Sulan continued, saying: "Gao Qi originally had no meritorious service and no standing reputation among the public; formerly, out of fear of death, he presumptuously killed Hushahu—this was merely done out of desperation.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan continued: "Gao Qi had no meritorious service and no standing among the public; formerly, out of fear for his life, he presumptuously killed Hushahu—this was merely an act of desperation.

sentences.zh: 一旦得志，妒賢能，樹奸黨，竊弄國權，自作威福。

translations.literal: Once he obtained his aim, he envied the able, planted a clique of scoundrels, usurped state power, and made his own prestige and benedictions.
translations.idiomatic: Once he obtained his aim, he envied the able, planted a clique of scoundrels, usurped state power, and made his own prestige and favors.

sentences.zh: 去歲，都下書生樊知一者詣高琪言：'颭軍不可信，恐終作亂。

translations.literal: Last year the capital student Fan Zhiyi went to Gao Qi and said, 'The Gust Troops cannot be trusted—they will surely finally raise rebellion.'
translations.idiomatic: Last year a capital student named Fan Zhiyi went to Gao Qi and said, 'The Gust Troops cannot be trusted—they will surely rebel in the end.'

sentences.zh: '遂以刀杖決殺之，自是無複敢言軍國利害者。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he had him beaten to death with staff and blade, and from that time forward none again dared speak of what benefited or harmed the army and state.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thereupon he had him beaten to death with staff and blade, and from that day forward none dared speak of what benefited or harmed the army and state.

sentences.zh: 宸聰之不通，下情之不達，皆此人罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor's keen hearing being blocked, and lower sentiments not reaching him—all are this man's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: That the emperor's keen hearing is blocked and lower sentiments do not reach him—all are this man's crimes.

sentences.zh: 及颭軍為變，以黨人塔不也為武甯軍節度使往招之，已而無成，則複以為武衛軍使。

translations.literal: When the Gust Troops mutinied, he sent his clique-member Tabuye as military commissioner of the Wuning Army to go entice them; when this afterward failed, he then again made him military commissioner of the Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gust Troops mutinied, he sent his clique-member Tabuye as military commissioner of the Wuning Army to entice them; when that failed, he then made him military commissioner of the Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 塔不也何人，且有何功，而重用如此。

translations.literal: Who is Tabuye, and what merit has he, that he should be so heavily employed?
translations.idiomatic: Who is Tabuye, and what merit has he, that he should be so heavily favored?

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，此賊變亂紀綱，戕害忠良，實有不欲國家平治之意。

translations.literal: In your subject's view, this scoundrel perverts and throws the institutions into disorder, slays the loyal and good, and in truth has the intention of not wishing the state to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: In your subject's view, this villain perverts institutions, slays the loyal and good, and in truth does not wish the state to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 昔東海時，胡沙虎跋扈無上，天下知之，而不敢言，獨台官烏古論德升、張行信彈劾其惡，東海不察，卒被其禍。

translations.literal: In the time of the Marquis of Donghai, Hushahu was overbearing above all, all under Heaven knew it yet none dared speak—only the investigative censors Wugulun Desheng and Zhang Xingxin impeached his wickedness; the Marquis of Donghai did not perceive this, and in the end suffered his calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Marquis of Donghai's time, Hushahu was overbearing above all; all under Heaven knew it yet none dared speak—only the investigative censors Wugulun Desheng and Zhang Xingxin impeached his wickedness; the Marquis of Donghai did not perceive it, and in the end suffered his calamity.

sentences.zh: 今高琪之奸，過於胡沙虎遠矣。

translations.literal: Now Gao Qi's wickedness far surpasses Hushahu's.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gao Qi's wickedness far surpasses Hushahu's.

sentences.zh: 台諫職當言責，迫於凶威，噤不敢忤。

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance offices have the duty to speak, yet they are forced by fierce authority and gag their mouths, not daring to disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate and remonstrance offices have the duty to speak out, yet they are cowed by his fierce authority and gag their mouths, not daring to disobey.

sentences.zh: 然內外臣庶見其恣橫，莫不扼腕切齒，欲一剚刃，陛下何惜而不去之耶。

translations.literal: Yet inner and outer officials and commoners, seeing his arbitrary violence, none do not clench their fists and grit their teeth, wishing to stab him with a blade once—why does Your Majesty spare him and not remove him?
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials and commoners within and without, seeing his arbitrary violence, clench their fists and grit their teeth, wishing to run him through with a blade—why does Your Majesty spare him and not remove him?

sentences.zh: 臣非不知言出而患至，顧臣父子迭仕聖朝，久食厚祿，不敢偷安。

translations.literal: Your subject is not unaware that words once spoken bring calamity, but your subject's father and son in succession have served the sagely dynasty, long receiving generous salaries—your subject does not dare seek ease in security.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is not unaware that words once spoken bring calamity, but your subject's father and son have served this sagely dynasty in succession and long received generous salaries—your subject does not dare seek ease in security.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下斷然行之，社稷之福也。

translations.literal: Only that Your Majesty resolutely carry this out—that is the blessing of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Only that Your Majesty act resolutely—that will be the blessing of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此乃大事，汝敢及之，甚善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This is a great matter; you dare touch on it—very good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "This is a grave matter; that you dare speak of it is excellent.

sentences.zh: 」素蘭複奏：「丞相福興，國之勳舊，乞召還京，以鎮雅俗，付左丞彖多以留後事，足也。

translations.literal: " Sulan again memorialized: "Grand Councilor Fuxing is an old meritorious subject of the state—I beg summon him back to the capital to steady refined custom, and entrust rear matters to Vice Grand Councilor Tuoduo—that is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: " Sulan again memorialized: "Grand Councilor Fuxing is an old meritorious servant of the state—I beg that he be summoned back to the capital to steady refined custom, and that rear matters be entrusted to Vice Grand Councilor Tuoduo—that would be sufficient.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「如卿所言，二人得無相惡耶？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As you say, would the two men not hate each other?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "As you say, would the two men not come to hate each other?

sentences.zh: 」素蘭曰：「福興、彖多同心同德，無不協者。

translations.literal: " Sulan said: "Fuxing and Tuoduo share one heart and one virtue—there is nothing discordant between them.
translations.idiomatic: " Sulan said: "Fuxing and Tuoduo share one heart and one purpose—there is nothing discordant between them.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「都下事殷，恐丞相不可輟。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Affairs at the capital are pressing—perhaps the Grand Councilor cannot be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Affairs at the capital are pressing—perhaps the Grand Councilor cannot be spared.

sentences.zh: 」素蘭曰：「臣聞朝廷正則天下正，不若令福興還，以正根本。

translations.literal: " Sulan said: "Your subject has heard that when the court is upright, all under Heaven is upright—it would be better to have Fuxing return to set the root aright.
translations.idiomatic: " Sulan said: "Your subject has heard that when the court is upright, all under Heaven is upright—it would be better to have Fuxing return and set the root aright.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「 朕徐思之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: " I shall think on this slowly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "I shall think on this at leisure.

sentences.zh: 」素蘭出，上複戒曰：「今日與朕對者止汝二人，慎無泄也。

translations.literal: " When Sulan left, the emperor again admonished him, saying: "Today those who spoke with me are only you two—take care that this is not leaked.
translations.idiomatic: " When Sulan left, the emperor again admonished him: "Today those who spoke with me are only you two—take care that this is not leaked.

sentences.zh: 」厥後，上以素蘭屢進直言，命再任監察御史。

translations.literal: " After this, because Sulan repeatedly offered straight words, he was ordered to serve again as investigative censor.
translations.idiomatic: " After this, because Sulan repeatedly offered straight counsel, he was ordered to serve again as investigative censor.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，言：「臣近被命體問外路官，廉幹者擬不差遣，若懦弱不公者罷之，具申朝廷，別議擬注。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, he said: "Your subject was recently ordered to assess officials on outer circuits—in the case of honest and capable ones, to recommend that they not be reassigned; in the case of those weak and unworthy or unfair, to dismiss them and report in full to the court for separate deliberation and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, he said: "Your subject was recently ordered to assess officials on outer circuits—for the honest and capable, to recommend that they not be reassigned; for the weak, unworthy, or unfair, to dismiss them and report in full to the court for separate deliberation and appointment.

sentences.zh: 臣伏念彼懦弱不公之人雖令罷去，不過止以待闕者代之，其能否又未可知，或反不及前官，蓋徒有選人之虛名，而無得人之實跡。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that although those weak, unworthy, and unfair persons are ordered dismissed, it amounts only to stopping them and having someone in waiting for a vacancy replace them—their capacity or incapacity is again unknown, and they might on the contrary be inferior to the former official, so that there is merely the empty reputation of selecting men, without the solid trace of obtaining men.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject reflects that although those weak, unworthy, and unfair officials are ordered dismissed, it amounts only to stopping them and having someone waiting for a vacancy replace them—their capacity is again unknown, and they might prove inferior to the former official, so that we have merely the empty reputation of selecting men, without the solid trace of obtaining the right men.

sentences.zh: 古語曰：'縣令非其人，百姓受其殃。

translations.literal: An ancient saying runs: 'If the magistrate is not the right man, the common people suffer his harm.'
translations.idiomatic: An ancient saying runs: 'If the magistrate is not the right man, the common people suffer his harm.'

sentences.zh: '今若後官更劣，則為患滋甚，豈朝廷恤民之意哉？

translations.literal: ' If a successor official is worse, then the harm will grow all the more severe—how can this be the court's intention to pity the people?
translations.idiomatic: ' If a successor is worse, the harm will grow all the more severe—how can this be the court's intention to pity the people?

sentences.zh: 夫守令，治之本也。

translations.literal: Magistrates and prefects are the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and prefects are the root of governance.

sentences.zh: 乞令隨朝七品、外路六品以上官，各舉堪充司縣長官者，仍明著舉官姓名，他日察其能否，同定賞罰，庶幾其可。

translations.literal: I beg that seventh-rank and above officials who attend court and sixth-rank and above on outer circuits each recommend those fit to serve as magistrates and prefects, still clearly stating the recommending official's name—later when their capacity or incapacity is inspected, rewards and punishments shall be fixed together—then perhaps it may be feasible.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that seventh-rank and above officials who attend court and sixth-rank and above on outer circuits each recommend those fit to serve as magistrates and prefects, clearly stating the recommender's name—later, when their capacity is inspected, let rewards and punishments be fixed together—then perhaps it may succeed.

sentences.zh: 議者或以閡選法、紊資品為言，是不知方今之事與平昔不同，豈可拘一定之法，坐視斯民之病而不權宜更定乎。

translations.literal: Debators may speak in terms of obstructing selection law and disordering rank grades, but this is not to understand that affairs today differ from ordinary times—how can one cling to a fixed law, sit watching this people's illness, and not weigh circumstances and revise?
translations.idiomatic: Debators may speak of obstructing selection law and disordering rank grades, but this fails to understand that affairs today differ from ordinary times—how can we cling to a fixed law, sit watching the people's suffering, and not weigh circumstances and revise?

sentences.zh: 」詔有司議行之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the responsible offices to deliberate and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the responsible offices to deliberate and carry it out.

sentences.zh: 時哀宗為皇太子，春宮所設師保贊諭之官多非其人，於是素蘭上章言：「臣聞太子者天下之本也，欲治天下先正其本，正本之要無他，在選人輔翼之耳。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Aizong was crown prince; the masters, protectors, and instructors appointed for the Eastern Palace were mostly not the right men. Thereupon Sulan submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that the crown prince is the root of all under Heaven; to govern all under Heaven one must first set this root aright, and of essentials for setting the root aright there is nothing else but selecting men to assist and shore him up.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Aizong was crown prince; the masters, protectors, and instructors appointed for the Eastern Palace were mostly not the right men. Thereupon Sulan submitted a memorial: "Your subject has heard that the crown prince is the root of all under Heaven; to govern the realm one must first set this root aright, and the essential means of setting the root aright is nothing other than selecting men to assist and shore him up.

sentences.zh: 夫生於齊者能齊言而不能楚語，未習之故也。

translations.literal: One born in Qi can speak the speech of Qi but cannot speak the speech of Chu—for one has not practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: One born in Qi can speak the speech of Qi but cannot speak the speech of Chu—for one has not practiced it.

sentences.zh: 人之性亦在夫習之而已。

translations.literal: Human nature also lies in what one practices.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature, too, lies in what one is taught to practice.

sentences.zh: 昔成王在繈褓中，即命周、召以為師保，戒其逸豫之心，告以持守之道，終之功光文、武，垂休無窮。

translations.literal: In antiquity King Cheng, while still in swaddling clothes, at once ordered the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to be his master and protector, warned off his disposition to ease and pleasure, and informed him of the way to hold and guard—the end was that his achievement outshone Wen and Wu, and his blessing extends without end.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity King Cheng, while still in swaddling clothes, at once appointed the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao as his master and protector, warned off his disposition to ease and pleasure, and taught him the way to hold and guard the realm—in the end his achievement outshone King Wen and King Wu, and his blessing extends without end.

sentences.zh: 欽惟陛下順天人之心，預建春宮。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty reflect on this in accord with the hearts of Heaven and men, and beforehand establish the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty, in accord with the hearts of Heaven and men, have already established the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太子仁孝聰明出於天資，總制樞務固已綽然有餘，倘更選賢如周、召之儔者使之夾輔，則成周之治不足侔矣。

translations.literal: The crown prince's benevolence, filial piety, intelligence, and clarity stem from inborn nature; in overseeing pivotal affairs he is already more than ample—if still more one selects worthies comparable to the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to flank and assist him, then the governance of the Zhou period would not be worth matching.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's benevolence, filial piety, intelligence, and clarity stem from inborn nature; in overseeing pivotal affairs he is already more than ample—if still more one selects worthies comparable to the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to flank and assist him, then the governance of the Zhou would not be worth matching.

sentences.zh: 」上稱善。

translations.literal: " The emperor commended this as good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended this as excellent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢為內侍局直長，尋遷諫議大夫，進侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Direct Supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, soon transferred to Remonstrance Grandee, and advanced to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Direct Supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, soon transferred to Remonstrance Grandee, and advanced to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 興定二年四月，以蒲鮮萬奴叛，遣素蘭與近侍局副使內族訛可同赴遼東，詔諭之曰：「萬奴事竟不知果何如，卿等到彼當得其詳，然宜止居鐵山，若複遠去，則朕難得其耗也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xingding, because Puxian Wannu rebelled, Sulan was dispatched with the Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, a member of the imperial clan Eke, together to go to Liaodong. The edict instructed them, saying: "Wannu's affair in the end we still do not know how it truly is—when you arrive there you will surely get the details, but you should only remain at Mount Iron; if again you go far away, then I shall have difficulty obtaining reports of you.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Xingding, because Puxian Wannu rebelled, Sulan was dispatched with the Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, a member of the imperial clan named Eke, together to Liaodong. The edict instructed them: "We still do not know how Wannu's affair will truly turn out—when you arrive there you will surely learn the details, but you should remain only at Mount Iron; if you go far away again, I shall have difficulty obtaining reports from you.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「朕以訛可性頗率易，故特命卿偕行，每事當詳議之。

translations.literal: " It also said: "I consider Eke's disposition rather rash and easy—therefore I have especially ordered you to go together; on every matter you should deliberate fully.
translations.idiomatic: " It also said: "I consider Eke's disposition rather rash and easy—therefore I have especially ordered you to go together; on every matter you should deliberate fully.

sentences.zh: 」素蘭將行，上言曰：「臣近請宣諭高麗複開互市事，聞以詔書付行省必蘭出。

translations.literal: " When Sulan was about to depart, he memorialized, saying: "Your subject recently requested to proclaim to Goryeo reopening mutual markets—the matter is heard to have the imperial edict given to the Branch Secretariat to issue through Bilan.
translations.idiomatic: " When Sulan was about to depart, he memorialized: "Your subject recently requested that Goryeo be instructed to reopen mutual markets—I hear the imperial edict has been given to the Branch Secretariat to issue through Bilan.

sentences.zh: 若令行省就遣諭之，不過鄰境領受，恐中間有所不通，使聖恩不達於高麗，高麗亦無由知朝廷本意也。

translations.literal: If the Branch Secretariat sends notice on the spot to proclaim it, it amounts only to receiving it at the neighboring border—your subject fears that in the middle something will not get through, so that the sage benefaction does not reach Goryeo and Goryeo also has no way to know the court's fundamental intent.
translations.idiomatic: If the Branch Secretariat sends notice on the spot to proclaim it, it amounts only to receiving it at the neighboring border—your subject fears something will be lost in transmission, so that the imperial grace does not reach Goryeo and Goryeo has no way to know the court's fundamental intent.

sentences.zh: 況彼世為籓輔，未嘗闕臣子禮，如遣信使明持恩詔諭之，貸糧、開市二者必有一濟。

translations.literal: Moreover, they for generations have been a feudatory screen and have never failed in the ritual of subject and minister—if you dispatch a credentialed envoy clearly bearing the gracious edict to instruct them, of extending grain credit and opening markets one or the other will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they have for generations been a feudatory screen and have never failed in the ritual of subject and minister—if you dispatch a credentialed envoy clearly bearing the gracious edict to instruct them, of extending grain credit and opening markets one or the other will surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 苟俱不從，則其曲在彼，然後別議圖之可也。

translations.literal: If both refuse, then the fault lies on their side—after that separate deliberation on a plan may be made.
translations.idiomatic: If both refuse, the fault lies on their side—after that a separate plan may be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 」上是其言，於是遣典客署書表劉丙從行。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words; thereupon he dispatched Liu Bing, recorder of documents in the Bureau of Court Reception, to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words; thereupon he dispatched Liu Bing, recorder of documents in the Bureau of Court Reception, to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 及還，授翰林待制。

translations.literal: When they returned, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Awaiting Imperial Orders.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, he was appointed Hanlin Academician Awaiting Imperial Orders.

sentences.zh: 八月，權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，授京西司農卿，俄改司農大卿，轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, he was appointed Director of the Capital West Office of Agriculture, soon changed to Grand Director of Agriculture, and transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, he was appointed Director of the Capital West Office of Agriculture, soon changed to Grand Director of Agriculture, and transferred to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，權元帥右都監、參知政事，行省於京兆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year, he was made Acting Right Commander of the Army, Participating in Government Affairs, with a Branch Secretariat at Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year, he was made Acting Right Commander of the Army, Participating in Government Affairs, with a Branch Secretariat at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷金安軍節度使，兼同、華安撫使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jin'an Army, also Pacification Commissioner of Tong and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jin'an Army, also Pacification Commissioner of Tong and Hua.

sentences.zh: 既而召還朝，行至陝被圍，久之，亡奔行在，道中遇害。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back to court; when he reached Shan he was surrounded, and after a long time fled to the mobile court; on the road he met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned back to court; when he reached Shan he was surrounded, and after a long time fled to the mobile court; on the road he met a violent death.

sentences.zh: 素蘭蒞官以修謹得名，然苛細不能任大事，較之輩流頗可稱。

translations.literal: Sulan in taking office won a name for diligence and caution, yet being harsh and minute he could not bear great affairs; compared with others of his generation he could rather be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan won a reputation for diligence and caution in office, yet being harsh and minute he could not bear great affairs; compared with others of his generation he could rather be praised.

sentences.zh: 自擢為近侍局直長，每進言多有補益。

translations.literal: From his promotion as Direct Supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, on every memorial he often had beneficial effect.
translations.idiomatic: From his promotion as Direct Supervisor of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, his memorials often had beneficial effect.

sentences.zh: 其居父喪，不飲酒，廬墓三年，時論以為難。

translations.literal: When he observed mourning for his father he did not drink wine, and dwelt by the tomb in a hut for three years—the age's opinion held this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When he observed mourning for his father he did not drink wine and dwelt by the tomb in a hut for three years—contemporary opinion held this difficult.

sentences.zh: 陳規，字正叔，絳州稷山人。

translations.literal: Chen Gui, style name Zhengshu, was a man of Jishan in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui, style name Zhengshu, was a native of Jishan in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年詞賦進士，南渡為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang he passed the poetry-and-rhapsody metropolitan examination; after the southward migration he became Investigative Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang he passed the poetry-and-rhapsody metropolitan examination; after the southward migration he became Investigative Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年十一月，上章言：「參政侯摯初以都西立功，獲不次之用，遂自請鎮撫河北。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhenyou, he submitted a memorial, saying: "Participating in Government Hou Zhi at first won extraordinary appointment through meritorious service on the western capital defense, and thereupon himself requested to pacify Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhenyou, he submitted a memorial: "Participating in Government Hou Zhi at first won extraordinary appointment through meritorious service defending the western capital, and thereupon himself requested to pacify Hebei.

sentences.zh: 陛下遽授以執政，蓋欲責其報效也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty hastily invested him in government affairs—surely you meant to charge him with repayments of effect.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty hastily invested him in government affairs—surely you meant to charge him with repayment in service.

sentences.zh: 既而盤桓西山，不能進退，及召還闕，自當辭避，乃恬然安居，至於按閱倉庫，規畫榷酤，豈大臣所宜親。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he lingered on West Mountain, unable to advance or retreat; when summoned back to the capital he ought to have declined and withdrawn, yet he calmly dwelt in security, even to the point of inspecting granaries and storehouses and planning the monopoly of wine—how is this what a great minister ought personally to do?
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward he lingered on West Mountain, unable to advance or retreat; when summoned back to the capital he ought to have declined and withdrawn, yet he calmly dwelt in security, even inspecting granaries and storehouses and planning the wine monopoly—how is this what a great minister ought personally to do?

sentences.zh: 方今疆土日蹙，將帥乏人，士不選練，冗食猥多，守令貪殘，百姓流亡，盜賊滋起，災變不息，則當日夜講求其故，啟告陛下者也，而摯未嘗及之。

translations.literal: At present the territory daily shrinks, generals and commanders are lacking, scholars are not selected and drilled, redundant eaters are excessive in number, magistrates and prefects are greedy and cruel, the common people flee in exile, bandits and thieves rise in abundance, omens and calamities cease not—then day and night one ought to seek the causes and open report to Your Majesty, yet Zhi has never touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: At present the territory daily shrinks, generals and commanders are lacking, scholars are not selected and drilled, redundant eaters are excessive, magistrates and prefects are greedy and cruel, the common people flee in exile, bandits and thieves rise in abundance, omens and calamities cease not—then day and night one ought to seek the causes and report to Your Majesty, yet Zhi has never touched on this.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下特賜省察，量其才分別加任使，無令負天下之謗。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty especially to examine and measure, and according to his capacity separately to assign and employ him—do not let him bear the empire's blame.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish Your Majesty especially to examine and measure him, and according to his capacity separately assign and employ him—do not let him bear the empire's blame.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response.
translations.idiomatic: " No response was given.

sentences.zh: 又言：「警巡使馮祥進由刀筆，無他才能，第以慘刻督責為事。

translations.literal: He also said: "Alert-Patrol Commissioner Feng Xiang advanced through the writing knife and brush, with no other talent or ability—only making cruel severity in supervision and taxation his affair.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Alert-Patrol Commissioner Feng Xiang advanced through the writing knife and brush, with no other talent or ability—only making cruel severity in supervision and taxation his affair.

sentences.zh: 由是升職，恐長殘虐之風，乞黜退以勵餘者。

translations.literal: For this he was promoted—I fear it will lengthen the wind of cruelty and severity; I beg dismiss and remove him to encourage the rest.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted—I fear it will encourage the wind of cruelty and severity; I beg that he be dismissed and removed to encourage the rest.

sentences.zh: 」詔即罷祥職，且諭規曰：「卿知臣子之分，敢言如此，朕甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: " An edict at once dismissed Feng from office and moreover instructed Gui, saying: "You know a subject's division of duty and dare speak thus—very much do I commend you."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict at once dismissed Feng from office and moreover instructed Gui: "You know a subject's proper division of duty and dare speak thus—I commend you highly."

sentences.zh: 四年正月，上言：「伏見沿河悉禁物斛北渡，遂使河北艱食，人心不安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he memorialized, saying: "Your subject has seen that along the river grain staples northward crossing are entirely forbidden, so that Hebei suffers hard famine and hearts are not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, he memorialized: "Your subject has seen that along the river grain staples northward crossing are entirely forbidden, so that Hebei suffers hard famine and hearts are not at peace.

sentences.zh: 昔秦、晉為仇，一遇年饑則互輸之粟。

translations.literal: In antiquity Qin and Jin were enemies—yet whenever there was famine in a year they mutually transported grain to each other.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Qin and Jin were enemies—yet whenever famine struck in a given year they mutually transported grain to each other.

sentences.zh: 今聖主在上，一視同仁，豈可以一家之民自限南北，坐視困餒而不救哉。

translations.literal: Now a sage ruler is above, regarding all with equal benevolence—how can one, for a single family's people, self-limit north and south, sit watching distress and famine and not rescue?
translations.idiomatic: Now a sage ruler is above, regarding all with equal benevolence—how can we, for a single family's people, self-limit north and south, sit watching distress and famine and not rescue them?

sentences.zh: 況軍民效死禦敵，使複乏食，生亦何聊，人心一搖，為害不細。

translations.literal: Moreover army and people die in effect defending the enemy—if again they lack food, what pleasure is there in living; once popular hearts waver, the harm is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when soldiers and civilians give their lives fighting the enemy, to leave them hungry again makes life scarcely worth living; once popular feeling wavers, the harm will be no small matter.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜於大陽、孟津等渡委官閱視，過河之物，每石官收不過其半，則富有之家利其厚息，輻湊而往，庶幾公私俱足。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks it appropriate at Dayang, Mengjin, and other crossings to commission officials to inspect; for goods crossing the river, let the official levy per shi not exceed half—then wealthy households will profit from ample returns and converge to go; perhaps both public and private will be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that officials be appointed to oversee crossings such as Dayang and Mengjin; for goods ferried across the river, let the state levy no more than half per shi in fees. Wealthy households would then be drawn by the prospect of ample profit to bring supplies in volume, so that public and private needs might both be met.

sentences.zh: 」宰執以河南軍儲為重，詔兩渡委官取其八，二以與民，至春澤足，大兵北還，乃依規請。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers, giving weight to Henan military stores, issued an edict that at both crossings commissioned officials should take eight-tenths and leave two-tenths for the people; only when spring marshes were full and the main army had returned north did they adopt Gui's request.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, giving priority to grain stores for the army in Henan, issued an edict that at both crossings commissioned officials should take eight-tenths of the levy and leave two-tenths for the people. Only when the spring floods had passed and the main northern army had returned did the court adopt Gui's proposal in full.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 三月，上言：「臣因巡按至徐州。

translations.literal: In the third month, he memorialized, saying: "Your subject, while conducting an inspection tour, reached Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he memorialized: "While conducting an inspection tour, your subject reached Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 去歲河北紅襖盜起，州遣節度副使紇石烈鶴壽將兵討之，而乃大掠良民家屬為驅，甚不可也。

translations.literal: Last year Red Coat bandits rose in Hebei; the prefecture sent Assistant Military Commissioner Geshilie He Shou to lead troops to suppress them, yet he greatly plundered common people's families as pressed labor—very much not allowable.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Red Coat rebels rose in Hebei; the prefecture sent Assistant Military Commissioner Geshilie He Shou to lead troops against them, yet he seized large numbers of civilians and their families as forced carriers—conduct that cannot be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 乞明敕有司，凡鶴壽所虜俱放免之，余路軍人有掠本國人為驅者，亦乞一體施行，庶幾河朔有所系望，上恩無有極已。

translations.literal: I beg clear orders to the relevant offices: all whom He Shou captured release and exempt; wherever soldiers on other routes have plundered our own people as pressed labor, I also beg uniform implementation—perhaps then Hebei north will have something to look to, and superior grace will be without limit.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the throne clearly instruct the relevant offices to release every person He Shou seized; wherever soldiers on other routes have seized our own people as pressed labor, the same measure should apply equally. Thus the people north of the Yellow River may have ground for hope in imperial favor without limit.

sentences.zh: 」事下尚書省，命徐州、歸德行院拘括放之，有隱匿者坐掠人為奴婢法，仍許諸人告捕，依令給賞，被虜人自訴者亦賞之。

translations.literal: " The matter was sent down to the Ministry of Revenue, ordering Xuzhou and Guide to establish courts to round up and release them; those who concealed faced the law on seizing people as slaves and maidservants; still permitted all people to report and arrest, with rewards according to regulations; captives who pleaded on their own behalf were also rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Revenue, which ordered Xuzhou and Guide to set up tribunals to locate captives and release them. Concealers were punished under the statute on seizing people as slaves and maidservants; informers were allowed to report offenders and receive rewards as prescribed, and captives who appealed on their own behalf were also rewarded.

sentences.zh: 四月，上言：「河北瀕河州縣，率距一舍為一寨，籍居民為兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he memorialized, saying: "Along the Yellow River in Hebei, prefectures and counties for the most part set up one fort every thirty li and registered residents as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, he memorialized: "Along the Yellow River in Hebei, prefectures and counties for the most part established one fortified camp every thirty li and registered local residents as troops.

sentences.zh: 數寨置總領官一人，並以宣差從宜為名。

translations.literal: Several forts had one overall leader appointed, all styled "imperial commissioner acting at discretion."
translations.idiomatic: Several camps together had one overall commander, all bearing the title "imperial commissioner acting at discretion."

sentences.zh: 其人大抵皆閑官，義軍之長、偏裨之屬尤多無賴輩，征逐宴飲取給於下，日以為常。

translations.literal: These men for the most part were idle officials; among militia leaders and subordinate officers especially many were rascals, pursuing banquets and feasts and taking their supplies from those below—daily as their constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: These men were for the most part idle officials; among militia captains and junior officers there were especially many rascals who lived by roaming from feast to feast and extracting their upkeep from subordinates as a daily routine.

sentences.zh: 及敵至則伏匿不出，敵去騷擾如初。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived they hid and did not emerge; when the enemy left they harassed as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived they hid and refused to fight; when the enemy withdrew they preyed on the people as before.

sentences.zh: 此輩小人假以重柄，朝廷號令威權無乃太輕乎。

translations.literal: These petty men were falsely given heavy authority—is not the court's command and majesty perhaps too lightly regarded?
translations.idiomatic: To invest such petty men with heavy authority—is not the court's command and majesty treated too lightly?

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜皆罷之，第委宣撫司從宜措畫足矣。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks all should be abolished; it suffices to entrust planning to the Pacification Commissioner acting at discretion alone.
translations.idiomatic: I believe all these posts should be abolished; it is enough to leave discretionary planning to the Pacification Commission alone.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，上章言：

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, he submitted a formal memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 陛下以上聖寬仁之姿，當天地否極之運，廣開言路以求至論，雖狂妄失實者亦不坐罪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with supreme sagely lenient and humane bearing, faces the utmost adversity of heaven and earth, broadly opening paths of speech to seek utmost discourse—even the wild and reckless who miss the truth are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, endowed with supreme sagacity and humane forbearance, faces the utmost adversity of heaven and earth and has broadly opened channels of remonstrance to seek the fullest counsel; even those who speak wildly and miss the mark are not punished.

sentences.zh: 臣忝耳目之官，居可言之地，苟為緘默，何以仰酬洪造。

translations.literal: Your subject disgracedly holds the office of eyes and ears, dwelling in a place where one may speak—if I keep silent, how may I requite the great creation?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds the disgraceful honor of serving as the throne's eyes and ears and occupies a post where speech is expected; if I remain silent, how can I repay your vast beneficence?

sentences.zh: 謹條陳八事，願不以人微而廢之，即無可采，乞放歸山林以懲屍祿之罪。

translations.literal: Respectfully I enumerate eight items; I wish they not be discarded because the person is slight. If none may be adopted, I beg to be released to mountain forests to punish the crime of drawing salary as a corpse.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth eight proposals and beg that they not be rejected because the speaker is insignificant. If none can be adopted, I beg to be sent home to the hills to atone for the offense of holding office without earning my stipend.

sentences.zh: 一曰責大臣以身任安危。

translations.literal: First: Require grand ministers personally to bear safety and danger.
translations.idiomatic: First: Hold the chief ministers personally responsible for the state's safety and peril.

sentences.zh: 今北兵起自邊陲，深入吾境，大小之戰無不勝捷，以致神都覆沒，翠華南狩，中原之民肝腦塗地，大河以北莽為盜區。

translations.literal: Now the northern troops have risen from the border marches and penetrated deep into our territory; in battles great and small there has been no lack of victory, leading to the divine capital's overthrow, the imperial carriage's southern hunt, the central plain's people with liver and brains smeared on the ground, and north of the great river the wilds turned into a bandit district.
translations.idiomatic: The northern armies have now risen on the frontier and driven deep into our realm; in battle after battle, large and small, they have known only victory, until the sacred capital fell, the imperial carriage fled south, the people of the central plains were slaughtered wholesale, and north of the Yellow River the wilderness became a realm of bandits.

sentences.zh: 臣每念及此，驚怛不已。

translations.literal: Whenever your subject thinks of this, I am startled and distressed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, I am shaken with unceasing dread.

sentences.zh: 況宰相大臣皆社稷生靈所系以安危者，豈得不為陛下憂慮哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the chief ministers and grandees are those on whom the altars of state and the living people depend for safety and danger—how can they fail to worry on Your Majesty's behalf?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the chief ministers are those on whom the altars of state and the lives of the people depend for safety and peril—how can they fail to share Your Majesty's anxieties?

sentences.zh: 每朝奏議，不過目前數條，特以碎末，互生異同，俱非救時之急者。

translations.literal: At each court session the deliberations extend no further than a few present items, merely trivial fragments on which they generate mutual differences—none are what urgently saves the times.
translations.idiomatic: At each court session their deliberations go no further than a handful of immediate items—mere trivia on which they quarrel among themselves—none of it what the age urgently requires.

sentences.zh: 況近詔軍旅之務，專委樞府，尚書省坐視利害，泛然不問，以為責不在己，其於避嫌周身之計則得矣，社稷生靈將何所賴。

translations.literal: Moreover, a recent edict entrusted military affairs exclusively to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Ministry of Revenue sits watching advantage and harm, broadly not inquiring, thinking the responsibility is not on themselves—for schemes to avoid suspicion and preserve the body they succeed, but on what will the altars of state and the living people rely?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a recent edict has entrusted military affairs exclusively to the Bureau of Military Affairs, while the Ministry of Revenue sits by watching advantage and harm and broadly declines to inquire, on the ground that the duty is not theirs. They succeed in the art of avoiding suspicion and saving their own skins—but on what are the altars of state and the people to rely?

sentences.zh: 古語雲：「疑則勿任，任則勿疑。

translations.literal: An old saying runs: "If you doubt, do not employ; if you employ, do not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: An old saying runs: "If you doubt a man, do not employ him; if you employ him, do not doubt him.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「謀之欲眾，斷之欲獨。

translations.literal: " It also says: "In planning, seek the many; in deciding, seek the solitary.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "In planning, seek many counsels; in deciding, keep decision in one hand.

sentences.zh: 」陛下既以宰相任之，豈可使親其細而不圖其大者乎。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty has already entrusted them as chief ministers—how can you let them attend to the small and not scheme for the great?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already entrusted them as chief ministers—how can you let them busy themselves with minutiae and not plan for the larger design?

sentences.zh: 伏願特同睿斷，若軍伍器械、常程文牘即聽樞府專行，至於戰守大計、征討密謀皆須省院同議可否，則為大臣者知有所責，而天下可為矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty especially to share in sagely decision: if army rosters, weapons, and routine documents, let the Bureau of Military Affairs execute them exclusively; as for grand plans of war and defense and secret schemes of campaign and suppression, all must be jointly deliberated by the ministries and the Bureau for approval or rejection—then those who serve as grand ministers will know they bear responsibility, and the realm may yet be saved.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to apply your sage judgment: routine matters of troops, arms, and paperwork may be left to the Bureau of Military Affairs alone, but grand strategy for offense and defense and secret plans for campaigns must be debated jointly by the ministries and the Bureau. Then the chief ministers will know they are accountable, and the realm may yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 二曰任台諫以廣耳目。

translations.literal: Second: Employ the censorate and remonstrance officials to broaden eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Empower the censorate and remonstrance officials to extend the throne's eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 人主有政事之臣，有議論之臣。

translations.literal: A ruler has ministers of administration and ministers of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler has ministers who administer affairs and ministers who debate policy.

sentences.zh: 政事之臣者宰相執政，和陰陽，遂萬物，鎮撫四夷，親附百姓，與天子經綸于廟堂之上者也。

translations.literal: Ministers of administration are the chief ministers who govern: harmonizing yin and yang, completing the myriad things, pacifying the four barbarians, drawing the people close—those who with the Son of Heaven weave policy in the hall of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of administration are the chief ministers who govern: harmonizing yin and yang, sustaining the myriad things, pacifying the four quarters, and drawing the people near—those who with the Son of Heaven weave statecraft in the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 議論之臣者諫官御史，與天子辨曲直、正是非者也。

translations.literal: Ministers of discourse are remonstrance officials and censors, who with the Son of Heaven distinguish crooked from straight and rectify right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of discourse are remonstrance officials and censors, who help the Son of Heaven distinguish right from wrong and set crooked matters straight.

sentences.zh: 二者豈可偏廢哉。

translations.literal: How can the two be one-sidedly abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: How can either be neglected?

sentences.zh: 昔唐文皇制中書門下入閣議事皆令諫官隨之，有失輒諫。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang decreed that whenever the heads of the Secretariat and Chancellery entered the privy council to deliberate affairs, remonstrance officials should accompany them; on any fault they at once remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang decreed that whenever the heads of the Secretariat and Chancellery entered the privy council to deliberate, remonstrance officials were to accompany them and speak up immediately at any fault.

sentences.zh: 國朝雖設諫官，徒備員耳，每遇奏事皆令回避。

translations.literal: Our dynasty, though it has established remonstrance officials, they are merely placeholder posts; whenever matters are reported they are all ordered to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has remonstrance officials in name, but they are mere placeholders; whenever business is reported at court they are ordered to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 或兼他職，或為省部所差，有終任不覿天顏、不出一言而去者。

translations.literal: Some hold other concurrent posts, some are detailed by ministries and departments; there are those who complete a term without beholding the imperial countenance and depart without uttering a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold other concurrent posts; some are detailed away by the ministries; there are men who complete a full term without ever seeing the emperor's face and leave without speaking a single word.

sentences.zh: 雖有御史，不過責以糾察官吏、照刷案牘、巡視倉庫而已，其事關利害或政令更革，則皆以為機密而不聞。

translations.literal: Though there are censors, they are charged only with investigating officials, auditing documents, and inspecting granaries; when affairs touch advantage and harm or policy orders are changed, all are deemed secret and not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Even the censors are charged only with investigating officials, auditing documents, and inspecting granaries; when matters touch vital interests or when policies are revised, everything is treated as confidential and they hear nothing.

sentences.zh: 萬一政事之臣專任胸臆、威福自由，或掌兵者以私見敗事機，陛下安得而知之。

translations.literal: In the ten-thousandth case that ministers of administration rely solely on their own breasts, wielding authority and blessing freely, or those who hold troops ruin the opportunity of affairs through private views—how would Your Majesty come to know?
translations.idiomatic: If ministers of administration should act solely on private impulse, wielding power as they please, or if commanders of troops should ruin strategic opportunity through personal prejudice—how would Your Majesty ever learn of it?

sentences.zh: 伏願遴選學術訁夾博、通曉世務、骨鯁敢言者以為台諫，凡事關利害皆令預議，其或不當，悉聽論列，不許兼職及充省部委差，苟畏徇不言則從而黜之。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that men of learning learned and comprehensive, versed in worldly affairs, and stern-boned and daring in speech be selected as censors and remonstrators; all matters touching advantage and harm should be made to include them in prior deliberation; if anything is improper, fully permit debate and enumeration; concurrent posts and detailing by ministries and departments are not permitted; if they fear and yield and do not speak, then dismiss them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that men of solid learning, broad and comprehensive knowledge, practical understanding of affairs, and moral courage be chosen as censors and remonstrators; let them take part in advance deliberation on every matter of public consequence, and where policy is wrong, allow full debate. Bar concurrent appointments and ministry detailing; if they shrink from speaking out, dismiss them at once.

sentences.zh: 三曰崇節儉以答天意。

translations.literal: Third: Honor frugality to answer heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Third: Uphold frugality to respond to heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 昔衛文公乘狄人滅國之余，徙居楚丘，才革車三十兩，乃躬行儉約，冠大帛之冠，衣大布之衣，季年致騋牝三千，遂為富庶。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Wen of Wei, riding on the remainder after the Di people destroyed his state, moved to dwell at Chuqiu with only thirty war chariots; then he personally practiced thrift, wearing a cap of great silk and garments of great cloth; in his late years he obtained three thousand chestnut mares and thus became wealthy and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Wen of Wei, after the Di destroyed his state, resettled at Chuqiu with only thirty war chariots; he then practiced austerity in person, wearing a coarse silk cap and plain cloth robes; in his later years he raised three thousand brood mares and made his state prosperous.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝承秦、項戰爭之後，四海困窮，天子不能具鈞駟，乃示以敦樸，身衣弋綈，足履革舄，未幾天下富安，四夷鹹服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, inheriting after the wars of Qin and Xiang, found the four seas exhausted and poor—the Son of Heaven could not assemble four horses of the same color; he then displayed solid simplicity, personally wearing coarse silk and on his feet leather sandals; before long the realm was wealthy and secure and the four barbarians all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, inheriting the realm after the wars of Qin and Xiang Yu, found the empire destitute—the emperor could not even match a team of four horses of one color. He set an example of plain living, wearing coarse silk himself and leather sandals on his feet; before long the realm grew rich and secure and the four quarters submitted.

sentences.zh: 國家自兵興以來，州縣殘毀，存者複為土寇所擾，獨河南稍完，然大駕所在，其費不貲，舉天下所奉責之一路，顧不難哉。

translations.literal: Our state since warfare arose—prefectures and counties lie in ruins; those that survive are again harassed by local bandits; only Henan is somewhat intact, yet where the great carriage dwells the expense is incalculable, and all that the realm supplies is charged to a single circuit—is this not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Since war broke out, prefectures and counties have been laid waste; where any survive, local bandits harass them again. Only Henan remains somewhat intact, yet wherever the imperial entourage resides the cost is beyond reckoning, and everything the realm can supply is levied on a single circuit—is that not a crushing burden?

sentences.zh: 賴陛下慈仁，上天眷佑，蝗災之餘而去歲秋禾、今年夏麥稍得支持。

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty's humane kindness and heaven's favoring care, after the locust disaster last year's autumn grain and this year's summer wheat have somewhat been sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's humane kindness and heaven's favor, after the locust plague last autumn's grain and this summer's wheat have barely sufficed to sustain us.

sentences.zh: 夫應天者要在以實，行儉者天必降福，切見宮中及東宮奉養與平時無異，隨朝官吏、諸局承應人亦未嘗有所裁省。

translations.literal: Now, to answer heaven lies in being substantial; those who practice thrift—heaven is sure to send blessing. Your subject has closely seen that provisions for the palace and Eastern Palace are no different from ordinary times; attendant court officials and all bureau service personnel likewise have never been reduced.
translations.idiomatic: To respond to heaven one must act in earnest; those who practice thrift heaven is sure to bless. I see plainly that upkeep for the palace and Eastern Palace is unchanged from peacetime, and the court attendants and bureau staff have never been cut back.

sentences.zh: 至於貴臣、豪族、掌兵官，莫不以奢侈相尚，服食車馬惟事紛華。

translations.literal: As for eminent ministers, powerful clans, and officers who hold troops—none fail to vie in luxury; food, drink, and carriages and horses pursue only splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Among eminent ministers, powerful clans, and military commanders, none fail to vie in luxury; food, dress, carriages, and horses pursue only display.

sentences.zh: 今京師鬻明金衣服及珠玉犀象者日增於舊，俱非克己消厄之道。

translations.literal: Now in the capital those who sell bright-gold garments and pearls, jade, rhinoceros horn, and ivory increase daily over the past—all are not the way of restraining oneself and dispelling calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, sellers of gilded garments, pearls, jade, rhinoceros horn, and ivory grow more numerous every day—none of this is the way to restrain desire and dispel disaster.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以衛文公、漢文帝為法，凡所奉之物痛自樽節，罷冗員，減浮費，戒豪侈，禁戢明金服飾，庶皇天悔禍，太平可致。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to take Duke Wen of Wei and Emperor Wen of Han as models: in all provisions for the court severely restrain yourself, abolish redundant posts, reduce floating expenses, warn against arrogant luxury, forbid and restrain bright-gold garments and ornaments—perhaps then imperial heaven will repent of calamity and great peace may be attained.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take Duke Wen of Wei and Emperor Wen of Han as models: drastically cut court expenditure, abolish redundant posts, reduce wasteful spending, warn against arrogant luxury, and forbid gilded dress and ornaments—then perhaps heaven will relent and peace may be restored.

sentences.zh: 四曰選守令以結民心。

translations.literal: Fourth: Select prefects and magistrates to bind popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Choose worthy prefects and magistrates to secure the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 方今舉天下官吏軍兵之費、轉輸營造之勞，皆仰給河南、陝西。

translations.literal: At present the costs of officials, soldiers, and troops throughout the realm and the labor of transport and construction all depend on supplies from Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At present the entire realm's costs for officials and troops, transport, and construction all depend on Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 加之連年蝗旱，百姓薦饑，行賑濟則倉廩懸乏，免徵調則用度不足，欲其實惠及民，惟得賢守令而已。

translations.literal: Added to this are successive years of locusts and drought; the people suffer repeated famine; to carry out relief empties the granaries, to exempt levies leaves revenue insufficient—if one wishes real benefit to reach the people, only by obtaining worthy prefects and magistrates may it be done.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this are years of locusts and drought; the people suffer repeated famine. Relief work drains the granaries, while exempting levies leaves revenue short. Real benefit for the people depends solely on worthy prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 當賦役繁殷、期會促迫之際，若措畫有方則百姓力省而易辦，一或乖謬有不勝其害者。

translations.literal: When levies and corvée are numerous and deadlines press urgently, if planning is well ordered the people's effort is saved and matters are easy to complete; if once perverse and mistaken, there are those who cannot bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: When levies are heavy and deadlines tight, sound planning saves the people's strength and makes compliance easy; a single error can inflict harm beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 況縣令之弊無甚於今，由軍衛監當進納勞效而得者十居八九，其桀黠者乘時貪縱，庸懦者權歸猾吏。

translations.literal: Moreover, the abuses of county magistrates have never been worse than now: eight or nine in ten obtained their posts through military guards supervising delivery of tribute and recording merit in labor; the fierce and cunning seize the moment to plunder wantonly, the mediocre and timid surrender power to crafty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the abuses of county magistrates have never been worse than today: eight or nine in ten gained office through military guards who supervised tribute deliveries and recorded labor merit. The bold and cunning seize the moment to plunder; the mediocre and timid surrender power to crafty clerks.

sentences.zh: 近雖遣官廉察，治其奸濫，易其疲軟，然代者亦非選擇，所謂除狼得虎也。

translations.literal: Recently, though officials were sent for honest inspection to punish their corruption and replace the worn-out and weak, yet the replacements were also not selected—what is called driving off a wolf and getting a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Recently inspectors were sent to punish corruption and replace the incompetent, yet the replacements were not chosen any better—it is, as the saying goes, driving off a wolf only to get a tiger.

sentences.zh: 伏乞明敕尚書省，公選廉潔無私、才堪牧民者，以補州府官。

translations.literal: Your subject begs clear orders to the Ministry of Revenue publicly to select men honest and clean, without private bias, whose talent suffices to shepherd the people, to fill prefectural and circuit posts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg clear orders to the Ministry of Revenue to select openly men who are honest, impartial, and capable of governing the people, to fill prefectural and circuit posts.

sentences.zh: 仍清縣令之選，及責隨朝七品，外任六品以上官各保堪任縣令者一員，如他日犯贓並從坐。

translations.literal: Further clarify selection for county magistrates, and charge court officials of the seventh rank and external officials of the sixth rank and above each to guarantee one man fit to serve as county magistrate; if later he commits corruption, all are punished together.
translations.idiomatic: Further purify selection for county magistrates, and require court officials of the seventh rank and field officials of the sixth rank and above each to vouch for one man fit to serve as magistrate; if he later commits corruption, the guarantor shares the punishment.

sentences.zh: 其資歷已系正七品，及見任縣令者，皆聽寄理，俟秩滿升遷。

translations.literal: Those whose seniority already ties them to regular seventh rank, and present county magistrates, may all be permitted to hold office in absentia until their term is full and they are promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Those already qualified at the regular seventh rank and current magistrates may hold office in absentia until their term ends and they are promoted.

sentences.zh: 複令監察以時巡按，有不法及不任職者究治之，則實惠及民而民心固矣。

translations.literal: Again order the surveillance commissioners to tour and inspect on schedule; where there is lawlessness or failure in office, investigate and punish—then real benefit will reach the people and popular hearts will be firm.
translations.idiomatic: Let surveillance commissioners tour on schedule and punish lawlessness and incompetence—then real benefit will reach the people and popular loyalty will be secured.

sentences.zh: 五曰博謀群臣以定大計。

translations.literal: Fifth: Broadly consult the ministers to fix the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Consult the ministers broadly to settle the grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 比者徙河北軍戶百萬余口于河南，雖革去冗濫而所存猶四十二萬有奇，歲支粟三百八十余萬斛，致竭一路終歲之斂，不能贍此不耕不戰之人。

translations.literal: Recently more than a million mouths of Hebei military households were moved to Henan; though redundant and excessive persons were removed, those who remain still number over four hundred twenty thousand odd; yearly grain disbursement exceeds three million eight hundred thousand shi, exhausting a whole circuit's revenue for the entire year and still unable to support these people who neither plow nor fight.
translations.idiomatic: Recently more than a million people from Hebei military households were relocated to Henan. Though redundant persons were weeded out, over four hundred twenty thousand remain, consuming more than 3.8 million shi of grain yearly—draining an entire circuit's annual revenue and still unable to support people who neither farm nor fight.

sentences.zh: 雖無邊事，亦將坐困，況兵事方興，未見息期耶。

translations.literal: Even without border affairs they would sit in distress; how much more when military affairs are just rising and no end is in sight?
translations.idiomatic: Even without border troubles the state would be strained to the breaking point—how much more now that war is raging with no end in sight?

sentences.zh: 近欲分佈沿河，使自種殖，然遊惰之人不知耕稼，群飲賭博習以成風，是徒煩有司征索課租而已。

translations.literal: Recently it was proposed to distribute them along the river and let them plant for themselves, yet these roaming and idle people do not know farming; drinking in groups and gambling have become habitual practice—this merely troubles the relevant offices to collect land tax in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the plan was to distribute them along the river for self-cultivation, yet these idle drifters know nothing of farming; drinking and gambling in groups have become the norm—so officials are merely harassed to collect land tax to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 舉數百萬眾坐糜廩給，緩之則用闕，急之則民疲，朝遷惟此一事已不知所處，又何以待敵哉。

translations.literal: Several millions sit consuming granary supplies; if eased, revenue falls short; if pressed, the people are exhausted—the court on this one matter alone already does not know what to do; how then may we await the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Millions sit idle consuming state grain; ease the burden and funds run short; press hard and the people collapse. The court is already at a loss over this one issue—how then can we face the enemy?

sentences.zh: 是蓋不審于初，不計其後，致此誤也。

translations.literal: This is broadly failure to examine matters at the start and not calculate what follows, leading to this error.
translations.idiomatic: This stems from failing to think matters through at the outset and plan for consequences—a mistake that has brought us here.

sentences.zh: 使初遷時去留從其所願，則欲來者是足以自贍之家，何假官廩，其留者必有避難之所，不必強遣，當不至今日措畫之難。

translations.literal: If at the first relocation departure and stay had followed their wishes, then those who wished to come would have been households able to support themselves—why borrow official granaries? Those who stayed would have had places to avoid disaster and need not have been forcibly sent—probably we would not have reached today's difficulty in planning.
translations.idiomatic: If at the first relocation people had been free to stay or go as they wished, those who came would have been families able to support themselves without state grain, and those who stayed would have had refuges of their own without forced removal—we would not face today's planning crisis.

sentences.zh: 古昔人君將舉大事，則謀及乃心，謀及卿士、庶人、卜筮，乞自今凡有大事必令省院台諫及隨朝五品以上官同議為便。

translations.literal: In antiquity when a ruler was about to undertake a great matter, he consulted his own heart, consulted ministers and grandees, common people, and divination. Your subject begs that from now on, whenever there is a great matter, the ministries, the Bureau, the censorate and remonstrance officials, and court officials of the fifth rank and above must jointly deliberate—this would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a ruler undertook a great enterprise, he consulted his own heart, his ministers, the people, and the oracles. I beg that from now on every major decision require joint deliberation by the ministries, the Bureau, censors and remonstrators, and all court officials of the fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 六曰重官賞以勸有功。

translations.literal: Sixth: Value official rewards to encourage those with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Make official rewards weighty to encourage merit.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，屢沛覃恩以均大慶，不吝官爵以激人心，至有未滿一任而並進十級，承應未出職而已帶驃騎榮祿者，冗濫之極至於如此，複開鬻爵進獻之門，然則被堅執銳效死行陣者何所勸哉。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, repeatedly broad favors have been poured out to share in great celebration; rank and titles are not spared to stir hearts—there are even those who before completing one term advance ten ranks together, and service attendants before leaving probation already bear Biaoqi Glory and Salary; redundancy and excess reach such an extreme, and again the gate of selling offices and presenting tribute is opened—then by what are those who don armor, grasp sharp weapons, and die in effect in the ranks to be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, broad amnesties have been proclaimed again and again; ranks and titles have been lavished to stir loyalty—some men advance ten grades before finishing a single term, and clerks still in probation already bear honorary Biaoqi titles. Redundancy has reached such extremes, and the sale of offices and tribute-buying have been reopened—what incentive remains for men who don armor and die in the ranks?

sentences.zh: 官本虛名，特出於人主之口，而天下之人極意趨慕者，以朝廷愛重耳。
