translations.literal: Office is fundamentally an empty name, issued solely from the ruler's mouth; yet all under heaven strive with utmost intent to pursue and admire it because the court cherishes and esteems it.
translations.idiomatic: Office is in itself an empty title, uttered only by the sovereign's mouth; yet all under heaven strive after it because the court treats it as precious.

sentences.zh: 若不計勳勞，朝授一官，暮升一職，人亦將輕之而不慕矣。

translations.literal: If merit is not calculated and one office is granted in the morning and one rank raised in the evening, people will also come to treat them lightly and not admire them.
translations.idiomatic: If merit is ignored and offices are handed out morning and promotions evening, men will soon hold them cheap and cease to strive for them.

sentences.zh: 已然之事既不可咎，伏願陛下重惜將來，無使公器為尋常之具，功賞為僥倖所乘。

translations.literal: What is already done cannot be blamed; your subject wishes Your Majesty to cherish what is to come, not letting public instruments become ordinary tools or merit rewards be ridden by chance.
translations.idiomatic: What is past cannot be undone; I beg Your Majesty to cherish the future, not let public office become a common commodity or rewards for merit a prize for the lucky.

sentences.zh: 又今之散官動至三品，有司艱於遷授，宜於減罷八資內量增階數，易以美名，庶幾曆官者不至於太驟，而國家恩權不失之太輕矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, today's honorary offices commonly reach the third rank; the relevant offices find promotion difficult. It is appropriate within the eight abolished grades to measure and increase the number of steps and exchange them for fine names—perhaps then those who pass through offices will not advance too swiftly, and the state's favor and authority will not be lost as too light.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, honorary offices now commonly reach the third rank, making promotion difficult for the ministries. Within the eight abolished grades, increase the number of steps and give them finer names, so that advancement is not too rapid and the state's favor and authority are not unduly cheapened.

sentences.zh: 七曰選將帥以明軍法。

translations.literal: Seventh: Select generals and commanders to clarify military law.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: Choose generals and commanders to enforce military discipline.

sentences.zh: 夫將者國之司命，天下所賴以安危者也。

translations.literal: Now, a general is the state's arbiter of fate, on whom all under heaven rely for safety and danger.
translations.idiomatic: A general holds the fate of the state in his hands; all under heaven depend on him for safety and peril.

sentences.zh: 舉萬眾之命付之一人，呼吸之間以決生死，其任顧不重歟？

translations.literal: The lives of ten thousand masses are entrusted to one man; between breaths life and death are decided—is not the responsibility weighty?
translations.idiomatic: The lives of thousands are entrusted to one man; in the space of a breath he decides life and death—is his burden not immense?

sentences.zh: 自北兵入境，野戰則全軍俱殃，城守則闔郡被屠，豈皆士卒單弱、守備不嚴哉，特以庸將不知用兵之道而已。

translations.literal: Since the northern troops entered the borders, in field battle whole armies perish together; in city defense whole prefectures are slaughtered—is it all because soldiers are few and weak and defenses not strict? It is solely because mediocre generals do not know the way of employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Since the northern armies invaded, field battles have ended in the annihilation of whole armies and sieges in the massacre of entire prefectures. Is it because the troops are few and defenses lax? It is solely because mediocre commanders do not understand the art of war.

sentences.zh: 古語雲：「三辰不軌，取士為相。

translations.literal: An old saying runs: "When the three luminaries depart from their courses, take scholars to serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: An old saying runs: "When the three luminaries depart from their courses, take scholars to serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 四夷交侵，拔卒為將。

translations.literal: When the four barbarians invade together, pluck soldiers to serve as generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters invade together, pluck soldiers from the ranks to serve as generals.

sentences.zh: 」今之將帥，大抵先論出身官品，或門閥膏粱之子，或親故假託之流，平居則意氣自高，遇敵則首尾退縮，將帥既自畏怯，士卒夫誰肯前。

translations.literal: " Today's generals and commanders for the most part first discuss family background and official rank—either sons of eminent houses and fine grain, or streams of kin and friends falsely entrusted; in ordinary times their spirit is self-exalted, when they meet the enemy they shrink head and tail; since generals themselves are timid, which soldiers will be willing to advance?
translations.idiomatic: Today's commanders are chosen chiefly for pedigree and rank—sons of great clans and privileged families, or men advanced through kinship and patronage. In peace they swagger; in battle they shrink. When the generals themselves are cowards, what soldier will advance?

sentences.zh: 又居常裒刻，納其饋獻，士卒因之以擾良民而莫可制。

translations.literal: Moreover in ordinary times they are harsh and exacting, receiving their gifts and presents; soldiers thereby harass common people and none can control them.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times they are harsh and grasping, accepting bribes, and their soldiers harass civilians beyond control.

sentences.zh: 及率之應敵，在途則前後亂行，屯次則排門擇屋，恐逼小民，恣其求索，以此責其畏法死事，豈不難哉。

translations.literal: When they lead troops to meet the enemy, on the march front and rear march in disorder; when encamped they line up at doors and choose houses, terrifying and pressing common people and indulging their demands—on this basis to require them to fear law and die for duty, is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: When they lead men against the enemy, the column marches in disorder on the road; in camp they force their way into houses and terrorize civilians to satisfy their demands. To expect such men to respect the law and die for duty—is that not hopeless?

sentences.zh: 況今軍官數多，自千戶而上，有萬戶、有副統、有都統、有副提控，十羊九牧，號令不一，動相牽制。

translations.literal: Moreover, today military officers are numerous; from the chiliarch upward there are myriarchs, deputy commanders, supreme commanders, and deputy controllers—ten sheep, nine herdsmen; orders are not unified and they constantly restrain one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, military officers are now too numerous: above the chiliarch there are myriarchs, deputy commanders, supreme commanders, and deputy controllers—too many chiefs for too few tribes; orders conflict and commanders constantly thwart one another.

sentences.zh: 切聞國初取天下，元帥而下，惟有萬戶，所統軍士不下數萬人，專制一路，豈在多哉？

translations.literal: Your subject has closely heard that when the state at the beginning took the realm, below the marshal there were only myriarchs, each commanding no fewer than tens of thousands of soldiers and holding sole authority over one circuit—was the point in being numerous?
translations.idiomatic: I understand that when the dynasty first conquered the realm, below the marshal there was only the myriarch, each commanding tens of thousands and holding sole authority over a circuit—was multiplicity the aim?

sentences.zh: 多則難擇，少則易精。

translations.literal: If many, hard to choose; if few, easy to refine.
translations.idiomatic: Too many commanders are hard to choose from; fewer are easier to make excellent.

sentences.zh: 今之軍法，每二十五人為一謀克，四謀克為一千戶，謀克之下有蒲輦一人、旗鼓司火頭五人，其任戰者才十有八人而已。

translations.literal: Today's military law: every twenty-five men form one mouke; four mouke form one chiliarch; under the mouke are one puyan, five banner-and-drum clerks and fire-sergeants—the actual fighters are only eighteen men.
translations.idiomatic: Under present military law, every twenty-five men form one mouke; four mouke form one chiliarch. Under each mouke are one puyan, five banner clerks and fire-sergeants—only eighteen men are actual fighters.

sentences.zh: 又為頭目選其壯健以給使令，則是一千戶所統不及百人，不足成其隊伍矣。

translations.literal: Again the commanders select the strong and healthy for personal service—then one chiliarch commands fewer than a hundred men, insufficient to form his unit.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders further select the strongest men for personal service, so a chiliarch commands fewer than a hundred men—too few to form a proper unit.

sentences.zh: 古之良將常與士卒同甘苦，今軍官既有俸廩，又有券糧，一日之給兼數十人之用。

translations.literal: Ancient worthy generals often shared sweetness and bitterness with soldiers; today military officers have both salary grain and ration tickets—a single day's provision suffices for several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy generals of old shared hardship with their men; today officers receive salary grain and ration tickets, and one day's allowance feeds dozens.

sentences.zh: 將帥則豐飽有餘，士卒則饑寒不足，曷若裁省冗食而加之軍士哉。

translations.literal: Generals and commanders are abundantly full with surplus; soldiers are hungry and cold and insufficient—how much better to cut redundant consumption and add it to the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Commanders feast in plenty while soldiers hunger and freeze—how much better to cut redundant rations and give them to the troops?

sentences.zh: 伏乞明敕大臣，精選通曉軍政者，分詣諸路，編列隊伍，要必五十人為一謀克，四謀克為一千戶，五千戶為一萬戶，謂之散將。

translations.literal: Your subject begs clear orders to the grand ministers to select finely men versed in military administration, dispatch them to each circuit to arrange and list units—requiring fifty men per mouke, four mouke per chiliarch, five thousand chiliarchs per myriarch, styled "dispersed generals."
translations.idiomatic: I beg clear orders to the chief ministers to select men versed in military affairs and send them to each circuit to reorganize the forces: fifty men per mouke, four mouke per chiliarch, five chiliarchs per myriarch—these to be styled "dispersed generals."

sentences.zh: 萬人設一都統，謂之大將，總之帥府。

translations.literal: Per ten thousand men establish one supreme commander, called "great general," all subordinated to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For every ten thousand men appoint one supreme commander, called a "great general," all under the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數不足者皆並之，其副統、副提控及無軍虛設都統、萬戶者悉罷省。

translations.literal: Where numbers are insufficient, all are merged; deputy commanders, deputy controllers, and empty posts of supreme commander and myriarch without troops are all abolished and cut.
translations.idiomatic: Merge units that fall short of full strength; abolish all deputy commanders, deputy controllers, and empty supreme commander and myriarch posts without troops.

sentences.zh: 仍敕省院大臣及內外五品以上，各舉方略優長，武勇出眾、材堪將帥者一二人，不限官品，以充萬戶以上都統、元帥之職。

translations.literal: Further order ministry and Bureau grand ministers and internal and external officials of the fifth rank and above each to recommend one or two men superior in strategy, outstanding in martial valor, whose talent suffices for general and commander—without limit on official rank—to fill posts of myriarch and above, supreme commander and marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Further order ministry and Bureau ministers and all officials of the fifth rank and above, at court and in the provinces, each to recommend one or two men of superior strategy and outstanding martial valor fit for high command, without regard to rank, to fill posts from myriarch and supreme commander up to marshal.

sentences.zh: 千戶以下，選軍中有謀略武藝為眾所服者充。

translations.literal: Below the chiliarch, choose from the army men with strategy and martial skill whom the masses respect to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: For ranks below chiliarch, choose from the ranks men of proven strategy and martial skill whom the troops respect.

sentences.zh: 申明軍法，居常教閱，必使將帥明於奇正虛實之數，士卒熟於坐作進退之節。

translations.literal: Clarify military law; in ordinary times drill and review—generals and commanders must be clear on the numbers of orthodox and unorthodox, empty and full; soldiers skilled in the cadence of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Clarify military law and drill regularly, so that commanders master the doctrine of orthodox and unorthodox, empty and full formations, and soldiers master the drill of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating.

sentences.zh: 至於弓矢鎧仗須令自負，習於勞苦。

translations.literal: As for bows, arrows, armor, and weapons, they must be made to carry them themselves and become practiced in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Make them carry their own bows, arrows, armor, and weapons and accustom them to hardship.

sentences.zh: 若有所犯，必刑無赦。

translations.literal: If there is any offense, punishment without pardon is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Any violation must be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 則將帥得人，士氣日振，可以待敵矣。

translations.literal: Then generals and commanders will obtain the right men, army spirit will daily be roused, and one may await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Then the right commanders will be in place, morale will rise day by day, and the state may face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 八曰練士卒以振兵威。

translations.literal: Eighth: Drill soldiers to rouse military might.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: Train the troops to restore military power.

sentences.zh: 昔周世宗常曰：「兵貴精而不貴多，百農夫不能養一戰士，奈何朘民脂膏養此無用之卒。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou often said: "Troops value refinement and do not value numbers; a hundred farmers cannot support one fighting soldier—how may one pare the people's fat and grease to support these useless troops?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou often said: "Armies value quality, not quantity; a hundred farmers cannot support one fighting soldier—why then drain the people's substance to feed these useless troops?

sentences.zh: 苟健懦不分，眾何以勸。

translations.literal: If robust and timid are not distinguished, how may the masses be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: If the brave and the weak are not separated, how can the troops be roused to exert themselves?

sentences.zh: 」因大搜軍卒，遂下淮南，取三關，兵不血刃，選練之力也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made a great muster of army soldiers, then descended on Huainan, took the Three Passes, and the troops never bloodied blades—it was the force of selection and drill.
translations.idiomatic: " He then conducted a thorough muster of the troops, marched south into Huainan, and seized the Three Passes without a blade being blooded—the fruit of selection and training.

sentences.zh: 唐魏徵曰：「兵在以道禦之而已。

translations.literal: Tang's Wei Zheng said: "Troops lie in governing them by the Way alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng of Tang said: "Armies need only be governed by principle.

sentences.zh: 禦壯健足以無敵于天下，何取細弱以增虛數。

translations.literal: Governing the robust and strong suffices to be without match under Heaven—why take the slight and weak to increase empty numbers?
translations.idiomatic: Discipline the strong and they will be matchless under Heaven; why recruit the weak merely to inflate the rolls?

sentences.zh: 」比者凡戰多敗，非由兵少，正以其多而不分健懦，故為敵所乘，懦者先奔，健者不能獨戰而遂潰，此所以取敗也。

translations.literal: " In recent times every battle has mostly been lost—not because troops were few, but precisely because they were many yet robust and timid were not divided; thus the enemy took advantage: the timid fled first, the robust could not fight alone and so routed—this is why defeat was taken.
translations.idiomatic: " In recent battles we have lost again and again—not from too few troops, but from too many troops with no distinction between the valiant and the useless. The enemy exploits this: the timid flee first, the brave cannot fight alone, and the whole force collapses. That is how we lose.

sentences.zh: 今莫若選差習兵公正之官，將已籍軍人隨其所長而類試之。

translations.literal: Now none is better than selecting and dispatching officials versed in troops who are fair and upright, taking already registered soldiers and by their strengths classifying and testing them.
translations.idiomatic: The best course now is to appoint impartial officials skilled in military affairs, take men already on the rolls, and test them according to their specialties.

sentences.zh: 其武藝出眾者別作一軍，量增口糧，時加訓練，視等第而賞之。

translations.literal: Those whose martial arts are outstanding are set apart into one army, their rations increased in measure, trained from time to time, and rewarded according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: Men of exceptional martial skill should be formed into separate corps, given extra rations, drilled regularly, and rewarded by rank.

sentences.zh: 如此，則人人激厲，爭效所長，而衰懦者亦有可用之漸矣。

translations.literal: Thus every man will be roused and spurred, each striving to display his strength, and even the declining and timid will gradually have means of being used.
translations.idiomatic: In this way every man will be spurred to excel at what he does best, and even the weaker troops may gradually be made serviceable.

sentences.zh: 昔唐文皇出征，常分其軍為上中下，凡臨敵則觀其強弱，使下當其上，而上當其中，中當其下。

translations.literal: Formerly when Tang's Literary Emperor went on campaign, he always divided his army into upper, middle, and lower; whenever facing the enemy he observed their strength and weakness, making the lower match their upper, the upper match their middle, and the middle match their lower.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Emperor Taizong of Tang campaigned, he habitually divided his army into upper, middle, and lower echelons; on meeting the enemy he gauged their strength and posted his lower echelon against their upper, his upper against their middle, and his middle against their lower.

sentences.zh: 敵乘下軍不過奔逐數步，而上軍中軍已勝其二軍，用是常勝。

translations.literal: When the enemy exploited the lower army, they ran in pursuit no more than a few steps, while the upper and middle armies had already defeated their other two armies—by this he was constantly victorious.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy might chase his lower echelon only a few steps before his upper and middle echelons had already defeated their other two forces; thus he won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 蓋古之將帥亦有以懦兵委敵者，要在預為分別，不使混淆耳。

translations.literal: For ancient generals and commanders also had timid troops they committed to the enemy—the point lay in separating them beforehand and not letting them be confused.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient commanders too sometimes offered up weak troops to the enemy; the key was to separate them in advance and never let the ranks become mixed.

sentences.zh: 上覽書不悅，詔付尚書省詰之。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was displeased; he ordered it sent to the Ministry of Revenue for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with displeasure and ordered the Ministry of Revenue to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 宰執惡其紛更諸事，謂所言多不當。

translations.literal: The chief ministers detested his overturning all matters and said what he spoke was mostly improper.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers resented his proposals to overturn established practice and judged most of his advice inadmissible.

sentences.zh: 於是規惶懼待罪，詔諭曰：「朕始以規有放歸山林之語，故令詰之，乃辭以不職忌諱，意謂朕惡其言而怒也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gui, fearful and awaiting punishment, received an edict instructing: "I at first because Gui had words of returning him to mountains and forests, therefore ordered him interrogated; yet he declined on the taboo of his office, meaning he thought I detested his words and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thereupon awaited punishment in fear. An edict explained: "I had him questioned because he spoke of retiring to the hills, yet he pleaded the taboo of his office as if I hated his words and meant to punish him.

sentences.zh: 朕初無意加罪，其令御史台諭之。

translations.literal: I at first had no intent to add guilt; let the Censorate instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: I never intended to punish him. Let the Censorate reassure him of this.

sentences.zh: 」尋出為徐州帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: " Soon he was sent out as staff officer of the Xuzhou Marshal's command.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon transferred out as staff officer under the Xuzhou martial command.

sentences.zh: 正大元年，召為右司諫，數上章言事，尋權吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengda, summoned as Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat, repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs, soon acting Ministry of Personnel division chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhengda reign (1224), he was recalled as Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat, submitted memorial after memorial, and was soon made acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時詔群臣議修復河中府，規與楊雲翼等言：「河中今為無人之境，陝西民力疲乏，修之亦不能守，不若以見屯軍士量力補治，待其可守即修之未晚也。

translations.literal: At the time the edict summoned ministers to discuss restoring Hezhong Prefecture; Gui with Yang Yunyi and others spoke: "Hezhong is now a land without men; Shaanxi's people's strength is exhausted and weary—restore it and still it cannot be held. It is not like relying on currently stationed soldiers to repair by measure; when it can be held, then restore—no hurry."
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated restoring Hezhong Prefecture. Gui and Yang Yunyi argued: "Hezhong lies abandoned; Shaanxi is exhausted and cannot hold it even if rebuilt. Better to let the garrisons there make such repairs as they can and wait until the place is defensible before a full restoration."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事解職。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of an affair relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed on account of the affair.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部尚書趙伯成坐銓選吏員出身王京與進士王著填開封警巡判官見闕，為京所訟免官，規亦坐之。

translations.literal: Early, Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhao Bocheng, on account of selection, had clerk-origin Wang Jing and jinshi Wang Zhu fill the open post of Kaifeng patrol judge; sued by Jing and relieved of office—Gui also sat in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Director Zhao Bocheng of the Ministry of Personnel had been dismissed after Wang Jing, a clerk by origin, sued him for appointing Wang Jing and the jinshi Wang Zhu together to fill an open Kaifeng patrol-judge post; Gui was implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，改充補闕。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month, changed to fill the post of Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he was reassigned as Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 十二月，言將相非材，且薦數人可用者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, spoke that generals and ministers were not the right talent, and also recommended several men who could be used.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he declared that the generals and ministers lacked talent and recommended several men fit for service.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，規及台諫同奏五事：一，乞尚書省提控樞密院，如大定、明昌故事。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, Gui and the Censorate and remonstrators jointly memorialized five matters: First, beg the Ministry of Revenue to take control of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as in the precedents of Dading and Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year (1225), Gui and the censorate and remonstrators jointly submitted five proposals: first, that the Ministry of Revenue resume supervision of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as under the Dading and Mingchang precedents.

sentences.zh: 二，簡留親衛軍。

translations.literal: Second, select and retain the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Second, streamline and retain the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 三，沙汰冗軍，減行樞密院、帥府。

translations.literal: Third, sift out and cut redundant troops, reduce itinerant Bureaus of Military Affairs and marshal commands.
translations.idiomatic: Third, weed out redundant troops and reduce itinerant military bureaus and marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四，選大臣為宣撫使，招集流亡以實邊防。

translations.literal: Fourth, select grand ministers as pacification commissioners to gather exiles and fill the border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, appoint senior ministers as pacification commissioners to gather refugees and strengthen the frontier.

sentences.zh: 五，選官置所，議一切省減。

translations.literal: Fifth, select officials to establish offices and discuss cutting everything that can be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, appoint officials to a commission to review and reduce expenditures across the board.

sentences.zh: 略施行之。

translations.literal: These were briefly put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: These measures were partially adopted.

sentences.zh: 四月，以大旱詔規審理冤滯，臨發上奏：「今河南一路便宜、行院、帥府、從宜凡二十處，陝西行尚書省、帥府五，皆得以便宜殺人，冤獄在此，不在州縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on account of great drought the edict ordered Gui to examine and clear delayed wrongs; on the eve of departure he memorialized: "Now on the Henan circuit there are twenty places of discretionary authority, itinerant bureaus, marshal commands, and expedient offices; in Shaanxi there are five itinerant Ministries of Revenue and marshal commands—all may kill at discretion. Wrongful imprisonments lie here, not in prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, owing to severe drought, the emperor ordered Gui to review cases of wrongful imprisonment. Before setting out he memorialized: "On the Henan circuit there are twenty offices with discretionary power—expedient commissions, itinerant bureaus, marshal headquarters, and the like; in Shaanxi there are five itinerant ministries and marshal commands—all empowered to execute at will. The wrongful convictions lie with them, not with the prefectures and counties."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「雨水不時則責審理，然則職燮理者當何如？

translations.literal: " He also said: "If rain and water are untimely, then blame falls on the examiner of delays—what then should those whose office is to harmonize and regulate do?"
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "If the rains fail, the examiner of delayed cases is blamed—what then of those whose duty is to harmonize the elements?"

sentences.zh: 」上善其言而不能有為也。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words yet could not act on them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words but could do nothing about them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上召完顏素蘭及規入見，面諭曰：「宋人輕犯邊界，我以輕騎襲之，冀其懲創告和，以息吾民耳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor summoned Wanyan Sulan and Gui for audience and face-to-face instructed: "Song men lightly violate the border; I with light cavalry raid them, hoping they will be chastised and sue for peace, to give rest to our people—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor summoned Wanyan Sulan and Gui and told them in person: "The Song lightly violate our border; I raid them with light cavalry in the hope they will be chastened and sue for peace, to give my people rest—that is all."

sentences.zh: 宋果行成，尚欲用兵乎。

translations.literal: If Song truly makes peace, do you still wish to use troops?
translations.idiomatic: If the Song have indeed made peace, do you still wish to wage war?

sentences.zh: 卿等當識此意。

translations.literal: You ministers ought to recognize this intent.
translations.idiomatic: You must understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 」規進曰：「帝王之兵貴於萬全，昔光武中興，所征必克，猶言'每一出兵，頭須為白'。

translations.literal: " Gui advanced and said: "An emperor's troops value being ten thousand parts secure; formerly when Guangwu restored the realm, every campaign he sent was sure to conquer, yet he still said, 'Each time I send out troops, my hair must turn white.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Gui replied: "An emperor's armies must be utterly secure. Even Guangwu, in restoring the Han, won every campaign he undertook, yet he said, 'Each time I take the field, my hair turns white.'"

sentences.zh: 兵不妄動如此。

translations.literal: Troops are not rashly moved to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his reluctance to move troops rashly.

sentences.zh: 」上善之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，上召群臣喻以陝西事曰：「方春北方馬漸羸瘠，秋高大勢並來，何以支持。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, third month, the emperor summoned ministers to instruct them on Shaanxi affairs: "At spring the northern horses gradually grow lean and weak; in autumn the great forces will all come—how may we support it?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year (1227) the emperor summoned the ministers to discuss Shaanxi and said: "In spring the northern horses grow lean; when autumn comes the great enemy forces will arrive together—how can we hold out?"

sentences.zh: 朕已喻合達盡力決一戰矣，卿等以為如何？

translations.literal: I have already instructed Heda to exert his strength and settle on one decisive battle—what do you ministers think?
translations.idiomatic: I have already told Heda to fight one decisive battle with all his strength—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」又言和事無益，撒合輦力破和議，賽不言：「今已遣和使，可中輟乎。

translations.literal: " He also spoke that peace affairs were without benefit; Sahelian strove to break the peace talks; Sai Buyan said: "Peace envoys have already been sent—may they be halted midway?"
translations.idiomatic: " He also said peace talks were useless. Sahelian pressed hard to break off negotiations. Sai Buyan said: "We have already sent peace envoys—can we stop them midway?"

sentences.zh: 」餘皆無言，規獨進曰：「兵難遙度，百聞不如一見。

translations.literal: " The rest were all silent; Gui alone advanced and said: "Troops are hard to gauge from afar—a hundred hearings are not like one seeing."
translations.idiomatic: " The others were silent. Gui alone spoke: "War is hard to judge from afar—a hundred reports are not worth one look."

sentences.zh: 臣嘗任陝西官，近年又屢到陝西，兵將冗懦，恐不可用，未如聖料。

translations.literal: Your subject once served as a Shaanxi official; in recent years I have repeatedly gone to Shaanxi—the troops and commanders are redundant and timid; I fear they cannot be used, not as Your Majesty calculates.
translations.idiomatic: I once served in Shaanxi and have visited there repeatedly in recent years. The troops and commanders are bloated and timid; I fear they will not perform as Your Majesty expects.

sentences.zh: 」言未終，烏古論四和曰：「陳規之言非是，臣近至陝西，軍士勇銳，皆思一戰。

translations.literal: " Before the words ended, Wugulun Sihe said: "Chen Gui's words are not correct; your subject recently reached Shaanxi—the soldiers are brave and sharp, all longing for one battle."
translations.idiomatic: " Before he finished, Wugulun Sihe said: "Chen Gui is wrong. I have just been to Shaanxi—the troops are brave and eager, all longing for battle."

sentences.zh: 」監察御史完顏習顯從而和之，上首肯，又泛言和事。

translations.literal: " Investigating Censor Wanyan Xixian followed and harmonized with him; the emperor nodded assent and again spoke broadly of peace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Investigating Censor Wanyan Xixian seconded him. The emperor nodded and spoke again in general terms of peace.

sentences.zh: 規對曰：「和事固非上策，又不可必成，然方今事勢不得不然。

translations.literal: Gui replied: "Peace affairs are indeed not the superior stratagem, nor can they be sure to succeed, yet the present situation of affairs cannot but be so."
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied: "Peace is certainly not the best policy, nor can it be guaranteed, yet given the present situation we have no choice."

sentences.zh: 使彼難從，猶可以激厲將士，以待其變。

translations.literal: Even if they are hard to follow, still one may rouse and spur generals and soldiers, to await their change.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the enemy is hard to deal with, the talks may still rouse the troops while we wait for circumstances to change.

sentences.zh: 」上不以為然。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not deem it so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor disagreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，又令集議省中，欲罷和事，群臣多以和為便，乃詔行省斟酌發遣，而事竟不行。

translations.literal: The next day, he again ordered assembly for discussion in the Secretariat, wishing to abolish peace affairs; the ministers mostly took peace as convenient, so an edict ordered the itinerant office to deliberate and dispatch—and in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he convened the ministers again in the Secretariat, intending to abandon the peace talks; most favored peace, so he ordered the itinerant office to decide how to proceed—and in the end nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 十月，規與右拾遺李大節上章，劾同判大睦親事撒合輦諂佞，招權納賄及不公事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Gui with Right Remembrancer Li Dajie submitted a memorial impeaching Associate Commissioner of the Great Mudiqin Affairs Sahelian for flattery and fawning, usurping power and taking bribes, and unfair matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gui and Right Remembrancer Li Dajie memorialized against Sahelian, associate commissioner of the Great Mudiqin Affairs, charging him with flattery, abuse of power, bribery, and malfeasance.

sentences.zh: 由是撒合輦竟出為中京留守，朝廷快之。

translations.literal: Thereby Sahelian was at last sent out as Zhongjing garrison commander; the court was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sahelian was consequently transferred out as garrison commander of Zhongjing, to the court's relief.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，又與大節言三事：「一，將帥出兵每為近臣牽制，不得專輒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, second month, again with Dajie spoke three matters: "First, when generals and commanders go out with troops they are every time restrained by close attendants and cannot act on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year (1228) he and Dajie again submitted three proposals: "First, field commanders are constantly restrained by palace favorites and cannot exercise independent authority.

sentences.zh: 二，近侍送宣傳旨，公受賂遺，失朝廷體，可一切禁絕。

translations.literal: Second, close attendants who deliver edicts and transmit orders openly receive bribes and gifts, losing the court's dignity—all may be utterly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Second, palace attendants who carry imperial orders openly accept bribes, debasing the dignity of the court; this should be forbidden entirely.

sentences.zh: 三，罪同罰異，何以使人。

translations.literal: Third, guilt the same yet punishment different—how may one employ men?
translations.idiomatic: Third, equal crimes receive unequal punishments—how can the law command respect?

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗嘗召文繡署令王壽孫作大紅半身繡衣，且戒以勿令陳規知。

translations.literal: Early, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned Brocade Office Director Wang Shousun to make a great red half-length embroidered robe, and admonished him not to let Chen Gui know.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Xuanzong had summoned Wang Shousun, director of the Brocade Office, to make a great red half-length embroidered robe and warned him not to let Chen Gui know.

sentences.zh: 及成，進，召壽孫問曰：「曾令陳規輩知否？

translations.literal: When it was finished, presented, he summoned Shousun and asked: "Did you ever let Chen Gui and his sort know?"
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished and presented, he summoned Shousun and asked: "Did you let Chen Gui and his like know?"

sentences.zh: 」壽孫頓首言：「臣侍禁庭，凡宮省大小事不敢為外人言，況親被聖訓乎。

translations.literal: " Shousun knocked his head and said: "Your subject attends the forbidden court; all great and small affairs of palace and Secretariat I dare not speak to outsiders—how much more when personally receiving sage instruction?"
translations.idiomatic: " Shousun kowtowed and said: "I serve within the palace precincts; I dare not speak of any matter, great or small, to outsiders—how much less when I have received Your Majesty's personal command?"

sentences.zh: 」上因歎曰：「陳規若知，必以華飾諫我，我實畏其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon sighed: "If Chen Gui knew, he would surely remonstrate me with ornament and splendor—I truly fear his words."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed and said: "If Chen Gui knew, he would surely remonstrate me against such finery—I truly dread his words."

sentences.zh: 」蓋規言事不假借，朝望甚重，凡宮中舉事，上必曰：「恐陳規有言。

translations.literal: " For Gui spoke on affairs without borrowing or sparing; court expectation was very heavy—whenever the palace undertook anything, the emperor would say: "I fear Chen Gui will have words."
translations.idiomatic: " Gui spoke his mind without reserve and commanded great respect at court; whenever the palace undertook anything, the emperor would say, "I fear Chen Gui will have something to say."

sentences.zh: 」一時近臣切議，惟畏陳正叔耳，挺然一時直士也。

translations.literal: " For a time close ministers in private discussion feared only Chen Zhengshu—he stood forthright as the upright man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: " For a time the palace favorites whispered among themselves that they feared only Chen Zhengshu; he stood out as the upright man of his generation.

sentences.zh: 後出為中京副留守，未赴，卒，士論惜之。

translations.literal: Later sent out as Zhongjing deputy garrison commander; before he arrived, he died—men of learning lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed deputy garrison commander of Zhongjing but died before taking up the post; scholars mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 規博學能文，詩亦有律度。

translations.literal: Gui was broadly learned and able in letters; his poetry also had measure and rule.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was broadly learned and skilled in prose; his poetry too was well wrought.

sentences.zh: 為人剛毅質實，有古人風，篤於學問，至老不廢。

translations.literal: As a man he was firm, resolute, plain, and solid, with the air of ancients; devoted to learning, to old age he did not abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: In character he was firm, plain, and solid, with the bearing of the ancients, and devoted to scholarship to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 渾源劉從益見其所上八事，歎曰：「宰相材也。

translations.literal: Hunyuan's Liu Congyi, seeing the eight matters he submitted, sighed: "Material for a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi of Hunyuan, reading his eight memorial proposals, exclaimed: "This is the stuff of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」每與人論及時事輒憤惋，蓋傷其言之不行也。

translations.literal: " Whenever he discussed current affairs with others he would grow indignant and regretful—for he grieved that his words were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he discussed current affairs with others he grew indignant and sorrowful, grieving that his counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，諫官稱許古、陳規，而規不以訐直自名，尤見重雲。

translations.literal: After the southern crossing, remonstrating officials were famed as Xu Gu and Chen Gui, yet Gui did not make a name for himself by accusatory bluntness and was especially esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, the remonstrators most famed were Xu Gu and Chen Gui; Gui did not trade on blunt accusation and was especially esteemed.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無一金，知友為葬之。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, the household had not one cash; friends and acquaintances buried him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his household had not a single coin; friends and acquaintances paid for his burial.

sentences.zh: 子良臣。

translations.literal: His son was Liangchen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liangchen.

sentences.zh: 許古，字道真，汾陽軍節度使致仕安仁子也。

translations.literal: Xu Gu, style Daozhen, was son of An Ren, retired military commissioner of the Fenyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gu, courtesy name Daozhen, was the son of An Ren, retired military commissioner of the Fenyang Army.

sentences.zh: 登明昌五年詞賦進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in rhapsody and prose in the fifth year of Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in rhapsody and prose in the fifth year of the Mingchang reign (1194).

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，自左拾遺拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, from Left Remembrancer he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyou era (1213) he was promoted from Left Remembrancer to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時宣宗遷汴，信任丞相高琪，無恢復之謀，古上章曰：

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuanzong moved to Bian, trusted Chief Minister Gao Qi, and had no plan for restoration—Gu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, he trusted Chief Minister Gao Qi and showed no plan for restoration. Gu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 自中都失守，廟社陵寢、宮室府庫，至於圖籍重器，百年積累，一朝棄之。

translations.literal: Since Zhongdu was lost, the temples and altars, imperial tombs, palaces and treasuries, down to maps, registers, and heavy vessels—a hundred years' accumulation—were abandoned in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhongdu fell, the temples and altars, imperial tombs, palaces and treasuries, even the maps, registers, and ritual vessels—a century's accumulation—were abandoned in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 惟聖主痛悼之心至為深切，夙夜思懼所以建中興之功者，未嘗少置也。

translations.literal: Only the sage lord's heart of bitter grief is utmost and deep; early and late he thinks and fears how to establish the merit of restoration—never for a moment laid aside.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grief is profound; day and night you ponder how to restore the dynasty—never for a moment has that purpose been set aside.

sentences.zh: 為臣子者食祿受責，其能無愧乎！

translations.literal: We who are ministers and sons eat salary and receive charge—how may we be without shame!
translations.idiomatic: We who hold office and draw salary—how can we not feel ashamed!

sentences.zh: 且閭閻細民猶顒望朝廷整訓師徒，為恢復計。

translations.literal: Moreover, common folk in lanes and alleys still look up in hope that the court will put in order and drill master and troops for a plan of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Even the common people in the lanes still look to the court to train the army and plan for restoration.

sentences.zh: 而今才聞拒河自保，又盡徙諸路軍戶河南，彼既棄其恆產無以自生，土居之民複被其擾，臣不知誰為此謀者。

translations.literal: Yet now one has only heard of holding the river to preserve oneself, and again moving all military households of every circuit to Henan—they having abandoned their constant property with no means to live, while native inhabitants are again disturbed by them; your subject does not know who made this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now we hear only of holding the Yellow River line and defending ourselves, while all military households from every circuit are moved wholesale to Henan. They have abandoned their livelihoods and cannot support themselves, and the local inhabitants are disturbed in turn. I do not know whose counsel this was.

sentences.zh: 然業已如是，但當議所以處之，使軍無妄費，民不至困窮則善矣。

translations.literal: Yet the affair is already thus; one should only discuss how to deal with it, so that the army has no reckless expenditure and the people do not reach destitution—then it is good.
translations.idiomatic: Since matters stand as they do, we should discuss how to manage them so that the army wastes nothing and the people are not driven to destitution.

sentences.zh: 臣聞安危所系，在於一相，孔子稱：「危而不持，顛而不扶，則將焉用？

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that what safety and peril hang upon lies in one chief minister; Confucius said: "In peril yet not upholding, toppling yet not supporting—of what use then is he?"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that safety and peril hang upon a single chief minister. Confucius said: "If in peril he does not uphold, if toppling he does not support—of what use is he?"

sentences.zh: 」事勢至此，不知執政者每對天顏，何以仰答清問也。

translations.literal: " Affairs have reached this point—I do not know how those who hold power, each time they face the heavenly countenance, can look up and answer the clear inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: " Affairs have come to this pass—I do not know how the chief ministers, when they face Your Majesty, can answer your searching questions.

sentences.zh: 今之所急，莫若得人，如前御史大夫裴滿德仁、工部尚書孫德淵，忠諒明敏，可以大用，近皆許告老，願複起而任之，必能有所建立以利國家。

translations.literal: What is urgent now is none so much as obtaining the right men—such as former Censor-in-Chief Puman Deren and Minister of Works Sun Deyuan, loyal, sincere, clear, and keen, who may be greatly employed; recently all were permitted to report old age—I beg they be raised again and entrusted, and they will surely be able to establish something to benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: What is urgent now is to find the right men. Former Censor-in-Chief Puman Deren and Minister of Works Sun Deyuan are loyal, sincere, and capable; both were recently permitted to retire. I beg that they be recalled and employed; they will surely accomplish something for the state.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕孫鐸，雖頗衰疾，如有大議猶可賜召，或就問之。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Sun Duo, though rather declined in illness, if there is great deliberation may still be granted summons, or one may go and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Duo, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, though aged and ill, may still be summoned for great deliberations, or the court may consult him in person.

sentences.zh: 人才自古所難，凡知治體者皆當重惜，況此耆舊，豈宜輕棄哉。

translations.literal: Talented men have from antiquity been hard to obtain; all who know the body of governance ought to value and cherish them—how much more these elders; how may they be lightly cast away?
translations.idiomatic: Talented men have always been hard to find; all who understand governance should cherish them—how much more these elders; they must not be lightly cast aside.

sentences.zh: 若乃臨事不盡其心，雖盡心而不明於理，得無益、失無損者，縱其尚壯，亦安所用。

translations.literal: As for those who in facing affairs do not exhaust their hearts, or though they exhaust their hearts yet are not clear on principle, gaining no benefit and losing no harm—even if they are still robust, of what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: As for those who do not devote themselves wholeheartedly to affairs, or who devote themselves but lack understanding of principle, who neither help nor harm—even if still vigorous, of what use are they?

sentences.zh: 方時多難，固不容碌碌之徒備員屍素，以塞賢路也。

translations.literal: The times are full of many hardships; one certainly cannot permit mediocre men to fill posts as dead weight, blocking the path of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In these troubled times we certainly cannot allow mediocre men to fill posts as dead weight and block the path of the worthy.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下宸衷剛斷，黜陟一新，以幸天下。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty's imperial heart be firm and decisive, dismissals and promotions entirely renewed, to bring fortune to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty be firm and decisive, renew appointments and dismissals entirely, and bring fortune to the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣前為拾遺時，已嘗備論擇相之道，乞取臣前奏並今所言，加審思焉。

translations.literal: When your subject was formerly Remembrancer, I already once fully discussed the Way of selecting a chief minister—I beg you take my former memorial together with what is spoken now and add careful thought.
translations.idiomatic: When I was Remembrancer I once fully discussed how to choose a chief minister. I beg Your Majesty to take my former memorial together with what I say now and ponder them carefully.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞將者民之司命，國家安危所系，故古之人君必重其選，為將者亦必以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that the general is the arbiter of life for the people, on whom the state's safety and peril hang; therefore ancient rulers always valued their selection, and those who become generals must also take all under Heaven as their own charge.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a general holds the people's lives in his hands and the state's safety hangs upon him; ancient rulers therefore prized their choice, and generals must take the realm as their personal charge.

sentences.zh: 夫將者貴謀而賤戰，必也賞罰使人信之而不疑，權謀使人由之而不知，三軍奔走號令以取勝，然後中心誠服而樂為之用。

translations.literal: For the general, stratagem is prized and battle is held cheap; rewards and punishments must make men trust without doubt, stratagems make men follow without knowing; the three armies run at orders to take victory—only then do they sincerely submit at heart and gladly be employed.
translations.idiomatic: A general values strategy over fighting; rewards and punishments must inspire unquestioning trust, stratagems must lead men without their knowing it; the three armies must rush to his orders to win—only then will they submit wholeheartedly and serve gladly.

sentences.zh: 邇來城守不堅，臨戰輒北，皆以將之不才故也。

translations.literal: In recent times city defense is not firm; on meeting battle they always flee north—all because the generals lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times garrisons have not held firm and armies have fled at the first clash—all because the commanders lack talent.

sentences.zh: 私於所昵，賞罰不公，至於眾怨，而懼其生變，則撫摩慰籍，一切為姑息之事。

translations.literal: They favor their intimates; rewards and punishments are not fair, until the masses resent them; fearing mutiny, they soothe and comfort with placating words—everything becomes indulgent appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: They favor their intimates and distribute rewards and punishments unfairly until the troops resent them; fearing mutiny, they soothe and placate them with indulgent concessions.

sentences.zh: 由是兵輕其將，將畏其兵，尚能使之出死力以禦敵乎？

translations.literal: Thus troops hold their generals light, and generals fear their troops—can they still make them exert death-dealing strength to repel the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Thus the troops despise their commanders and the commanders fear their troops—how can such men be made to fight to the death against the enemy?

sentences.zh: 願令腹心之臣及閑於兵事者，各舉所知，果得真才，優加寵任，由戰功可期矣。

translations.literal: I wish that trusted ministers and those versed in military affairs each recommend those they know; if true talent is truly obtained, favor and trust them abundantly—then through battle merit may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that trusted ministers and those versed in military affairs each recommend men they know; if true talent is found, honor and employ them generously—then victories may be expected.

sentences.zh: 如河東宣撫使胥鼎、山東宣撫使完顏弼、涿州刺史內族從坦，昭義節度使必蘭阿魯帶，或忠勤勇幹，或重厚有謀，皆可任之，以扞方面。

translations.literal: Such as Hedong Pacification Commissioner Xu Ding, Shandong Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Bi, Zhuozhou Prefect imperial clansman Cong Tan, Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Bilian Aludai—some loyal, diligent, brave, and capable, some grave, thick, and possessed of stratagem—all may be entrusted to defend the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Xu Ding, pacification commissioner of Hedong; Wanyan Bi, pacification commissioner of Shandong; Cong Tan of the imperial clan, prefect of Zhuozhou; and Bilian Aludai, military commissioner of Zhaoyi—some loyal, diligent, and brave, others grave and resourceful—all are fit to defend the regions.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 河北諸路以都城既失，軍戶盡遷，將謂國家舉而棄之，州縣官往往逃奔河南。

translations.literal: On the Hebei circuits, because the capital was already lost and military households were all moved, they took it that the state had lifted and abandoned them—prefectural and county officials often fled in flight to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hebei circuits, because the capital had fallen and all military households were relocated, officials took it that the state had abandoned them wholesale, and prefectural and county officers often fled south to Henan.

sentences.zh: 乞令所在根括，立期遣還，違者勿複錄用。

translations.literal: I beg orders to each place to search out and tally them, set a term for sending them back, and those who violate it not again be recorded and employed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that each locality hunt them down, set a deadline for their return, and never again employ those who disobey.

sentences.zh: 未嘗離任者議加恩賚，如願自效河北者亦聽陳請，仍先賞之，減其日月。

translations.literal: Those who never left their posts should be discussed for added grace and gifts; if they wish to offer themselves to Hebei, also permit them to state requests, still reward them first, and reduce their term of service.
translations.idiomatic: Those who never left their posts should receive added rewards; those who wish to serve in Hebei should be permitted to petition, rewarded in advance, and granted reduction in their term of service.

sentences.zh: 州縣長貳官並令兼領軍職，許擇軍中有才略膽勇者為頭目，或加爵命以收其心，能取一府者即授以府長官，州縣亦如之，使人懷複土之心。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county chief and deputy officials are all ordered to concurrently hold military posts; permit choosing from the army men of talent, stratagem, and daring courage as leaders, or adding noble ranks and orders to win their hearts—whoever can take one prefecture is at once granted that prefecture's chief post; prefectures and counties are likewise; make men harbor the heart of recovering their soil.
translations.idiomatic: Let prefectural and county chiefs and deputies all hold military posts concurrently; permit them to choose from the ranks men of talent and courage as unit leaders, or grant titles to win loyalty; whoever recaptures a prefecture should be made its chief, and the same for counties—so that men will cherish the hope of recovering their homeland.

sentences.zh: 別遣忠實幹濟者，以文檄官賞招諸脅從人，彼既苦於敵役，來者必多，敵勢當自削。

translations.literal: Separately send loyal, solid, and capable men; use written proclamations and official rewards to summon all coerced followers; they already suffering bitterly under enemy service, those who come will surely be many, and the enemy's strength should of itself be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Send out reliable and capable agents to recruit all who were coerced into the enemy ranks with proclamations and official rewards; once they weary of serving the foe, many will defect, and the enemy's strength will dwindle of itself.

sentences.zh: 有司不知出此，而但為清野計，事無緩急惟期速辦，今晚禾十損七八，遠近危懼，所謀可謂大戾矣。

translations.literal: The offices do not know to use this plan, but only make schemes for scorched-earth; affairs without urgency or delay solely expect swift completion—this evening's grain crops seven or eight parts in ten damaged, near and far alarmed and fearful; what is planned can be called greatly perverse.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities never thought of this, but pursued only a scorched-earth policy, treating every matter as urgent and rushing it through regardless; tonight seven or eight tenths of the ripening grain were lost, and alarm spread far and wide—the design could scarcely be more wrong-headed.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 京師諸夏根本，況今常宿重兵，緩急征討必由於此，平時尚宜優於外路，使百姓有所蓄積，雖在私室猶公家也。

translations.literal: The capital is the root of the myriad Xia; moreover now it constantly lodges heavy troops; urgency and ease in campaigns and punitive expeditions must go through this; in normal times it is still fitting to treat it better than the outer circuits, enabling the common people to have some accumulation—even in private chambers it is still the public household.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the foundation of the empire, and now heavy forces are stationed there permanently; every urgent campaign must pass through it. Even in peaceful times it should be favored over the provinces so that the people may build up stores—wealth held in private homes is still wealth for the state.

sentences.zh: 今有司搜括餘糧，致轉販者無複敢入，宜即止之。

translations.literal: Now the offices search and round up surplus grain, causing transport merchants no longer to dare enter—it is fitting to stop this at once.
translations.idiomatic: Now the authorities are seizing every scrap of surplus grain until grain merchants dare not bring supplies in at all. This ought to be halted immediately.

sentences.zh: 臣頃看讀陳言，見其盡心竭誠以吐正論者，率皆草澤疏賤之人，況在百僚，豈無為國深憂進章疏者乎？

translations.literal: Your subject recently looked through presented words, seeing those who exhaust heart and exhaust sincerity to speak forthright discourse—almost all are grass-swamp, remote, and base people; moreover among the hundred officials, how could there not be those who for the state in deep worry submit memorials?
translations.idiomatic: I have lately been reading submitted memorials; those who spoke their minds with full sincerity were almost all humble men from the grass roots. Among the full body of officials, are there none who harbor deep concern for the state and would submit memorials?

sentences.zh: 誠宜明敕中外，使得盡言不諱，則太平之長策出矣。

translations.literal: Truly it is fitting clearly to command within and without, enabling them to speak fully without taboo—then the long strategy for great peace will emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should clearly command the court and the realm to speak freely without restraint, and the grand design for lasting peace will appear of itself.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書省，略施行焉。

translations.literal: An edict handed it to the Department of State Affairs; it was briefly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the memorial to the Department of State Affairs, and it was put into effect in part.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書左司員外郎，兼起居注，無何，轉右司諫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Division Clerk of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Recorder of the Imperial Residence; before long he was promoted to Right Division Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to auxiliary clerk in the left division of the Department of State Affairs and made concurrent recorder of the imperial residence; before long he became remonstrator of the right division.

sentences.zh: 時丞相高琪立法，職官有犯皆的決，古及左司諫抹撚胡魯剌上言曰：「禮義廉恥以治君子，刑罰威獄以治小人，此萬世不易論也。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Minister Gao Qi made laws; officials who offended were all given bamboo floggings. Gu and Left Division Remonstrator Mo'nian Hulula submitted words, saying: "Rites, righteousness, integrity, and shame are used to govern gentlemen; punishments, authority, and prisons are used to govern petty men—this is discussion unchanging for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Minister Gao Qi legislated so that any offending official was flogged on the spot. Gu and Left Division Remonstrator Mo'nian Hulula submitted a memorial: "Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame govern gentlemen; punishment, coercion, and prison govern common men—this principle has never changed."

sentences.zh: 近者朝廷急於求治，有司奏請從權立法：職官有犯應贖者亦多的決。

translations.literal: Recently the court is urgent to seek good order; the offices memorialized requesting expedient lawmaking: officials who offended and should redeem were also mostly given bamboo floggings.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the court has been urgent for order, and the offices have asked for emergency legislation: even officials who ought by law to redeem their offenses with fines are instead flogged.

sentences.zh: 夫爵祿所以馭貴也，貴不免辱，則卑賤者又何加焉。

translations.literal: Titles and stipends are what are used to steer the noble; if the noble cannot escape humiliation, then upon the base and mean what further can be added?
translations.idiomatic: Rank and stipend exist to govern the eminent; if even the eminent cannot escape humiliation, what added sanction remains for the lowly?

sentences.zh: 車駕所駐非同征行，而凡科征小過皆以軍期罪之，不已甚乎。

translations.literal: Where the imperial carriage resides is not the same as campaign expeditions, yet every minor offense in tax collection and levies is punished by military deadlines—is this not already excessive?
translations.idiomatic: The place where the throne rests is not a battlefield, yet every petty offense in collection and levy is punished as a military crime—is this not excessive?

sentences.zh: 陛下仁恕，決非本心，殆有司不思寬靜可以措安，而專事督責故耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is humane and forgiving—this is certainly not your true heart; probably the offices do not think that lenience and quiet can settle peace, but single-mindedly pursue supervision and blame, that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is humane and forgiving; this cannot be your true intent. The offices perhaps do not believe that clemency and calm can bring peace, and so devote themselves wholly to harsh supervision.

sentences.zh: 且百官皆朝廷遴選，多由文行、武功、閥閱而進，乃與凡庶等，則享爵祿者亦不足為榮矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the hundred officials are all selected by the court, mostly advancing through literary conduct, military merit, or noble lineage—then to be made equal to common folk means that those who enjoy titles and stipends also are insufficient to count as honor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover every official is chosen by the court, advancing through learning, military merit, or noble lineage—to treat them like commoners is to make rank and stipend no honor at all.

sentences.zh: 抑又有大可慮者，為上者將曰官猶不免，民複何辭，則苛暴之政日行。

translations.literal: Moreover there is again what can greatly be worried over: those above will say, "If even officials cannot escape it, what plea have the people?"—then harsh and violent government advances day by day.
translations.idiomatic: There is a still graver concern: those in authority will say, "Even officials are not spared—what recourse have the common people?"—and harsh rule will grow worse each day.

sentences.zh: 為下者將曰彼既亦然，吾複何恥，則陵犯之心益肆。

translations.literal: Those below will say, "They are already the same—what further shame have I?"—then the heart of encroachment and offense grows more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Those below will say, "If they are no better than I, what shame is there in my act?"—and the spirit of defiance will run rampant.

sentences.zh: 其弊豈勝言哉。

translations.literal: Its harms—how could they be exhausted in words?
translations.idiomatic: The harm of this cannot be overstated.

sentences.zh: 伏願依元年赦恩'刑不上大夫'之文，削此一切之法，幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish to rely on the first-year amnesty grace, the text "punishment does not ascend to the grandees," and abolish this lump of laws—most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Your Majesty follow the first-year amnesty, which held that "punishment does not reach the great officers," and repeal these measures entirely—this would be a great blessing.

sentences.zh: 」上初欲行之，而高琪固執以為不可，遂寢。

translations.literal: " The Emperor at first wished to carry it out, but Gao Qi stubbornly held it could not be done, and it was put to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor at first wished to act on this, but Gao Qi stubbornly insisted it could not be done, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四年，以右司諫兼侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served as Right Division Remonstrator, concurrently Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the reign he held the post of right division remonstrator and served concurrently as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時大兵越潼關而東，詔尚書省集百官議，古上言曰：「兵逾關而朝廷甫知，此蓋諸將欺蔽罪也。

translations.literal: At the time the great army crossed Tong Pass going east; an edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to gather the hundred officials to deliberate. Gu submitted words, saying: "Troops passed the pass yet the court only now knows—this is probably the crime of the generals' deception and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army crossed Tong Pass and marched east, the Emperor ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene the officials for deliberation. Gu submitted a memorial: "The army crossed the pass before the court even learned of it—this is surely the generals' crime of concealing intelligence.

sentences.zh: 雖然，大兵駐閿鄉境，數日不動，意者恐吾河南之軍逆諸前，陝西之眾議其後，或欲先令覘者伺趨向之便，或以深入人境非其地利而自危，所以觀望未遽進也。

translations.literal: Although so, the great army is stationed on the Wenxiang border, several days without moving—probably they fear our Henan army will meet them ahead, Shaanxi masses will plot behind, or wish first to have scouts watch the convenience of trends, or because deep entry into others' territory is not its terrain advantage and they imperil themselves—therefore they watch and wait, not hastily advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the main force has camped at Wenxiang for days without moving. They likely fear our Henan army will block their front and our Shaanxi forces threaten their rear; they may wish first to send scouts to test our disposition, or they may know that deep penetration into hostile territory without local advantage puts them at risk—hence they hesitate and have not advanced swiftly.

sentences.zh: 此時正宜選募銳卒並力擊之，且開其歸路，彼既疑惑，遇敵必走，我眾從而襲之，其破必矣。

translations.literal: This time is precisely fitting to select and recruit sharp soldiers, join strength to strike them, and moreover open their road of return; they already doubtful, meeting the enemy will surely flee; our masses following to raid them—their defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the moment to raise picked troops and strike them with full force, while leaving their line of retreat open. Once they are thrown into doubt and meet our troops they will surely flee, and our forces can fall upon them—their defeat is certain.

sentences.zh: 」上以示尚書省，高琪沮其議，遂不行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor showed it to the Department of State Affairs; Gao Qi obstructed his deliberation, and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor showed the memorial to the Department of State Affairs; Gao Qi blocked the proposal, and nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 是月，始置招賢所，令古等領其事。

translations.literal: That month they first established the Office for Recruiting the Worthy, ordering Gu and others to lead its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That month the court first established the Office for Recruiting Talent and put Gu and others in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 興定元年七月，上聞宋兵連陷贛榆、漣水諸縣，且獲偽檄，辭多詆斥，因諭宰臣曰：「宋人構禍久矣，朕姑含容者，眾慮開兵端以勞吾民耳。

translations.literal: Xingding first year, seventh month—the Emperor heard Song troops in succession took Ganyu, Lianshui, and various counties, and moreover obtained a forged proclamation; its words mostly slandered and reviled. He thereupon instructed the chief ministers, saying: "The Song people have contrived calamity long; I for the moment bore it because all feared opening the military edge to toil our people."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xingding, the Emperor learned that Song forces had taken Ganyu, Lianshui, and other counties in succession, and had seized a forged proclamation full of abuse. He told his chief ministers: "The Song have long been stirring trouble; I have borne with them only because all feared that war would weary our people."

sentences.zh: 今數見侵，將何以處，卿等其與百官議。

translations.literal: Now repeatedly we see infringement—how shall we deal with it? You and others should with the hundred officials deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have violated us again and again—how shall we respond? Go and deliberate with the full body of officials."

sentences.zh: 」於是集眾議於都堂，古曰：「宋人孱弱，畏我素深，且知北兵方強，將恃我為遮罩，雖時跳樑，計必不敢深入，其侮嫚之語，特市井屠沽兒所為，烏足較之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they gathered collective deliberation at the metropolitan hall. Gu said: "Song people are weak and feeble, fearing us Jurchens deeply; moreover they know northern troops are just strong—they will rely on us as a screen and canopy. Though at times they leap about like dogs on the beam, their plan will surely not dare go deep; their insulting, scornful words are merely the doing of market ward butchers and peddlers—how could they suffice to be weighed?"
translations.idiomatic: " The court then assembled for deliberation in the metropolitan hall. Gu said: "The Song are feeble and have long feared us deeply; they know the northern armies are strong and will lean on us as their shield. They may prance about for a time, but they will not dare push deep inland. Their insulting language is the talk of market butchers and peddlers—hardly worth answering."

sentences.zh: 止當命有司移文，諭以本朝累有大造，及聖主兼愛生靈意。

translations.literal: One need only command the offices to send a dispatch, instructing them on how our dynasty repeatedly had great acts of creation, and the sage ruler's intent to love all living beings alike.
translations.idiomatic: We need only order the authorities to send them a dispatch, reminding them of the great favors our dynasty has repeatedly shown them and of the sage ruler's care for all living beings."

sentences.zh: 彼若有知，複尋舊好，則又何求。

translations.literal: If they have understanding, again seeking the old good relations—then what further is sought?
translations.idiomatic: If they have any sense, they will seek to restore the old friendship, and we need ask nothing more."

sentences.zh: 其或怙惡不悛，舉眾討之，顧亦未晚也。

translations.literal: If perchance they cling to wickedness without repentance, raising the masses to punish them—looking back, it also is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: If they cling to wickedness and will not mend, then we may raise the army against them—and even then it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」時預議者十餘人，雖或小異而大略則一，既而丞相高琪等奏：「百官之議，咸請嚴兵設備以逸待勞，此上策也。

translations.literal: " At the time those who took part in deliberation were more than ten men; though there were small differences, the great outline was one. Soon after, Chief Minister Gao Qi and others memorialized: "The hundred officials' deliberation—all request strict troops and set equipment, with ease awaiting their toil—this is the upper strategy."
translations.idiomatic: " More than ten officials took part in the debate; their views differed in small points but agreed in the main. Soon Chief Minister Gao Qi and others reported: "The officials unanimously urge strengthening defenses and holding our ground until the enemy wears himself out—that is the best policy."

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以諸路把軍官時有不和不聽，更相訴訟，古上言曰：「臣以為善者有勸，惡者有懲，國之大法也。

translations.literal: At the time the court, because prefectural route baojun officers sometimes had disharmony and disobedience, repeatedly sued and litigated one another, Gu submitted words, saying: "Your subject considers that for the good there should be encouragement, for the evil there should be punishment—this is the great law of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Because military governors in the circuits often quarreled and disobeyed one another, filing suits back and forth, Gu submitted a memorial: "I hold that the good should be rewarded and the wicked punished—this is the fundamental law of the state."

sentences.zh: 苟善惡不聞，則上下相蒙，懲勸無所施矣。

translations.literal: If good and evil are not heard, then above and below mutually conceal, and punishment and encouragement have nowhere to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: If good and evil go unreported, superiors and subordinates will deceive one another, and reward and punishment can never be applied."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor commended the proposal and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 古以朝廷欲舉兵伐宋，上疏諫曰：「昔大定初，宋人犯宿州，已而屢敗，世宗料其不敢遽乞和，乃敕元帥府遣人議之，自是太平幾三十年。

translations.literal: Gu, because the court wished to raise troops to attack Song, submitted a remonstrance memorial, saying: "In the past at the start of Dading, Song people invaded Suzhou; soon after they were repeatedly defeated. Emperor Shizong gauged that they would not dare hastily beg peace, and therefore ordered the Marshal's Office to send men to negotiate; from this peace lasted nearly thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished to raise an army against Song, Gu submitted a remonstrance memorial: "In the early Dading era the Song attacked Suzhou and were soon beaten repeatedly. Emperor Shizong judged they would not hasten to sue for peace and ordered the Marshal's Office to open negotiations; peace then lasted nearly thirty years."

sentences.zh: 泰和中，韓侂胄妄開邊釁，章宗遣駙馬僕撒揆討之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Han Tuozhou rashly opened border provocation; Emperor Zhangzong sent the imperial son-in-law Pusan Huai to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era Han Tuozhou rashly provoked war on the frontier, and Emperor Zhangzong sent his son-in-law Pusan Huai against them.

sentences.zh: 揆慮兵興費重不能久支，陰遣侂胄族人齎乃祖琦畫像及家牒，偽為歸附，以見丘崇，因之繼好，振旅而還。

translations.literal: Huai considered that when troops rise, expenses are heavy and cannot long be sustained; he secretly sent Tuozhou's clansmen bearing his grandfather Han Qi's portrait and household registers, falsely as submission, to meet Qiu Chong; by this continuing good relations, he struck the banners and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huai knew that war was costly and could not be sustained long; he secretly sent members of Tuozhou's clan bearing the portrait and genealogy of his grandfather Han Qi, pretending to offer submission, to Qiu Chong, and on this basis renewed friendly relations and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 夫以世宗、章宗之隆，府庫充實，天下富庶，猶先俯屈以即成功，告之祖廟，書之史冊，為萬世美談，今其可不務乎？

translations.literal: For such as emperors Shizong and Zhangzong at their height, treasuries full and solid, the realm wealthy and thriving—they still first bowed low to achieve success, announced it to the ancestral temple, wrote it in the historical records, as a beautiful tale for ten thousand generations—how can today not pursue this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Shizong and Zhangzong at the height of their power, with full treasuries and a prosperous realm, still humbled themselves to secure success, reported it to the ancestral temple, and recorded it in the histories as a deed celebrated for all time—how can we today fail to follow their example?

sentences.zh: 今大兵少息，若複南邊無事，則太平不遠矣。

translations.literal: Now the great army has slightly rested; if again the southern border has no affairs, then great peace is not far.
translations.idiomatic: The main armies have only just drawn breath; if the southern border can be kept quiet, peace is not far off.

sentences.zh: 或謂專用威武可使宋人屈服，此殆虛言，不究實用。

translations.literal: Some say that solely using martial might can make Song people submit—this is probably empty talk, not investigating practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that force alone will make the Song submit—that is hollow talk that ignores what is practicable.

sentences.zh: 借令時獲小捷，亦不足多賀。

translations.literal: Even granting that for the moment one obtains small victories, they are also insufficient to be much congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we win minor victories for a time, they are scarcely cause for rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 彼見吾勢大，必堅守不出，我軍倉猝無得，須還以就糧，彼複乘而襲之，使我欲戰不得、欲退不能，則休兵之期殆未見也。

translations.literal: They seeing our power great, will surely firmly defend and not come out; our army in haste obtains nothing, must return to seek grain, they again mount and raid us—making us wish to battle yet not obtain it, wish to withdraw yet cannot; then the term for resting troops is probably not yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: They will see our strength and cling to their defenses without coming out. Our army, finding nothing in a hasty campaign, must withdraw for supplies; they will then strike us in turn, leaving us unable to fight or retreat—and the day when our troops may rest will be far off indeed.

sentences.zh: 況彼有江南蓄積之餘，我止河南一路征斂之弊，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Moreover they have the surplus accumulation of Jiangnan; we only have the abuses of levies on the single Henan route—this can make one's heart cold.
translations.idiomatic: They have the stored wealth of Jiangnan behind them, while we rely on the exhausted levies of Henan alone—a thought to chill the heart.

sentences.zh: 願陛下隱忍包容，速行此策，果通知，則大兵聞之，亦將斂跡，以吾無掣肘故也。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty forbearance and tolerance, swiftly to carry out this strategy; if truly peace is made known, then the great army hearing of it will also draw in their tracks, because we have no tugging at the elbows.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to exercise forbearance and tolerance and swiftly pursue this course. If peace is truly announced, the northern armies will also restrain themselves, for we will no longer be tied down on two fronts.

sentences.zh: 河南既得息肩，然後經略朔方，則陛下享中興之福，天下賴涵養之慶矣。

translations.literal: Henan having obtained rest on the shoulders, then afterward planning and governing the northern regions—then Your Majesty enjoys the blessing of restoration, the realm relies on the congratulation of cherishing and nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Henan can breathe freely, we may then attend to the north; Your Majesty will enjoy the blessings of restoration and the realm the joy of nurture and repose.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下略近功、慮後患，不勝幸甚。

translations.literal: Only wishing Your Majesty to slight near-term achievement and consider later suffering—I cannot bear how fortunate this would be.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to set aside immediate gains and weigh the troubles that follow—nothing would be more fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」上是其言，即命古草議和牒文。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his words and at once ordered Gu to draft the peace dispatch document.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor approved his counsel and at once ordered Gu to draft the peace dispatch.

sentences.zh: 既成，以示宰臣，宰臣言其有哀祈之意，自示微弱，遂不用。

translations.literal: When it was finished, it was shown to the chief ministers; the chief ministers said it had the intention of grieving supplication, showing weakness of itself—and it was not used.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, it was shown to the chief ministers, who said it sounded pleading and weak and refused to use it.

sentences.zh: 監察御史粘割梭失劾榷貨司同提舉毛端卿貪污不法，古以詞理繁雜，輒為刪定，頗有脫漏，梭失以聞，削官一階，解職，特免殿年。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Niancie Suoshi impeached the Monopoly Goods Office co-administrator Mao Duanqing for corruption and lawlessness. Gu, because the wording and reasoning were prolix and complex, presumptuously revised and settled it—there were rather omissions and gaps. Suoshi reported it; Gu's rank was cut one step, office removed, specially exempted from palace audience for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Niancie Suoshi impeached Mao Duanqing, co-administrator of the Monopoly Goods Office, for corruption and malfeasance. Gu found the indictment prolix and revised it on his own, omitting several points. Suoshi reported this to the throne; Gu was demoted one rank, removed from office, and specially exempted from court attendance for one year.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，尚書省奏諫官闕員，因以古為請，上曰：「朕昨暮方思古，而卿等及之，正合朕意，其趨召之。

translations.literal: Third year, first month—the Department of State Affairs memorialized that remonstrating officials had vacant posts and therefore requested Gu. The Emperor said: "I only yesterday evening was thinking of Gu, and you and others reached it—this precisely fits my intent; hasten to summon him."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the Department of State Affairs reported vacancies among the remonstrators and nominated Gu. The Emperor said: "Only yesterday evening I was thinking of Gu, and you have brought him forward—it is exactly what I wished. Summon him at once."

sentences.zh: 」複拜左補闕。

translations.literal: " He was again appointed Left Remonstrator and Deficiency-Filler.
translations.idiomatic: " He was again appointed left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 八月，削官四階，解職。

translations.literal: Eighth month—his rank was cut four steps, office removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was demoted four ranks and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷遣近侍局直長溫敦百家奴暨刑部侍郎奧屯胡撒合徙吉州之民於丹以避兵鋒，州民重遷，遮道控訴，百家奴諭以天子恐傷百姓之意，且令召晉安兵將護老幼以行。

translations.literal: Initially the court sent Inner Attendance Bureau Direct Attendant Wendun Baijianu together with Ministry of Justice Vice Minister Aotun Husahé to move Jizhou's people to Dan to avoid the army's edge. The prefecture's people dreaded relocation, blocked the road, and petitioned in protest. Baijianu instructed them on the Son of Heaven's fear of harming the common people, and moreover ordered summoning Jin'an military officers and generals to escort old and young on the journey.
