translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had sent Wendun Baijianu, direct attendant of the Inner Attendance Bureau, together with Vice Minister of Justice Aotun Husahé to relocate the people of Jizhou to Dan to escape the fighting. The populace, dreading removal, blocked the road and lodged protests. Baijianu explained the Emperor's wish not to harm the people and ordered Jin'an troops to escort the old and young on the move.

sentences.zh: 眾意兵至則必見強也，乃噪入州署，索百家奴殺之。

translations.literal: The masses thought when troops arrived they would surely meet with coercion; thereupon they clamored into the prefectural offices, demanding Baijianu to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd believed that once troops arrived coercion would follow; they stormed the prefectural offices clamoring for Baijianu's death.

sentences.zh: 胡撒合畏禍，矯徇眾情，與之會飲歌樂盡日，眾肩舁導擁，歡呼拜謝而去。

translations.literal: Husahé feared calamity and falsely bent to the crowd's feelings; with them he met in drinking and song and music the whole day. The masses shoulder-carried and guided him in escort, shouting joy and bowing in thanks as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Husahé, fearing for his life, feigned sympathy with the mob, feasted and caroused with them all day, and was borne aloft on their shoulders amid shouts of joy as they let him go.

sentences.zh: 既還，詔古與監察御史紇石烈鐵論鞫之，諭旨曰：「百家奴之死，皆胡撒合所賣也，其閱實以聞。

translations.literal: When they returned, an edict ordered Gu together with Investigating Censor Heshelie Tielun to interrogate and try him, instructing: "Baijianu's death—all was sold by Husahé; verify the facts and report."
translations.idiomatic: On their return, an edict ordered Gu and investigating censor Heshelie Tielun to examine the case, with instructions: "Baijianu's death was Husahé's doing—establish the facts and report."

sentences.zh: 」奧屯胡撒合既下獄，上怒甚，亟欲得其情以正典刑，而古等頗寬縱之。

translations.literal: " Aotun Husahé, having entered prison, the Emperor was very angry and urgently wished to obtain the facts to apply the canonical punishment—but Gu and others were rather lenient and indulgent toward him.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Aotun Husahé was imprisoned the Emperor was furious and urgently wanted the full facts so that the statutory penalty might be applied, but Gu and his colleagues were unduly lenient.

sentences.zh: 胡撒合自縊死，有司以故出論罪，遂有是罰。

translations.literal: Husahé hanged himself; the offices because of the case submitted a judgment on guilt—thereupon came this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Husahé hanged himself; the authorities submitted a finding on the affair, and Gu received this punishment.

sentences.zh: 哀宗初即位，召為補闕，俄遷左司諫，言事稍不及昔時。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong first took the throne, Gu was summoned as Remonstrator and Deficiency-Filler; soon he was transferred to Left Division Remonstrator; his speaking on affairs was somewhat not equal to former times.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong first acceded, Gu was summoned as remonstrator and soon promoted to left division remonstrator, but his remonstrances no longer matched his former vigor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，居伊陽，郡守為起伊川亭。

translations.literal: Before long he retired from office, residing at Yiyang; the prefect built for him the Yichuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired and lived at Yiyang, where the prefect built for him the Yichuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 古性嗜酒，老而未衰，每乘舟出村落間，留飲或十數日不歸，及溯流而上，老稚爭為挽舟，數十裏不絕，其為時人愛慕如此。

translations.literal: Gu by nature was fond of wine; old yet not declining. Each time he took a boat out among villages and hamlets, he would stay drinking sometimes ten-odd days without returning. When he went upstream, old and young competed to tow his boat—for several tens of li without break; he was loved and admired by the people of the time like this.
translations.idiomatic: Gu loved wine and in old age had lost none of his appetite for it. He would take a boat among the villages and stay drinking for ten days or more without returning. When he rowed upstream, old and young alike competed to tow his boat for miles without end—such was the affection in which the people held him.

sentences.zh: 正大七年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: Zhengda seventh year he died, age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Zhengda, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 古平生好為詩及書，然不為士大夫所重，時論但稱其直雲。

translations.literal: Gu all his life was fond of making poetry and calligraphy, yet was not heavily esteemed by scholar-officials; opinion of the time only called him upright—that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Gu spent his life fond of poetry and calligraphy, yet won little esteem among the scholar-officials; contemporary opinion honored only his forthrightness.
